## Update an Organization Member's Team Role

<a id="opIdupdateOrganizationMemberTeam"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/members/string/teams/string/' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "teamRole": "contributor"
  }'
```

`PUT /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/members/{member_id}/teams/{team_id_or_slug}/`

The relevant organization member must already be a part of the team.

Note that for organization admins, managers, and owners, they are
automatically granted a minimum team role of `admin` on all teams they
are part of. Read more about [team roles](https://docs.sentry.io/product/teams/roles/).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "teamRole": "contributor"
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-organization-members-team-role-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|member_id|path|string|true|The ID of the organization member to change|
|team_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the team the resource belongs to.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» teamRole|body|string|false|The team-level role to switch to. Valid roles include:<br><br>* `contributor` - Contributors can view and act on events, as well as view most other data within the team's projects.<br>* `admin` - Admin privileges on the team. They can create and remove projects, and can manage the team's memberships.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» teamRole|contributor|
|» teamRole|admin|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "isActive": true,
  "teamRole": "admin"
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-organization-members-team-role-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<h3 id="update-an-organization-members-team-role-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|isActive|boolean|true|none|none|
|teamRole|string|true|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|teamRole|contributor|
|teamRole|admin|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
auth_token
</aside>

## Add an Organization Member to a Team

<a id="opIdaddOrganizationMemberTeam"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/members/string/teams/string/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/members/{member_id}/teams/{team_id_or_slug}/`

This request can return various success codes depending on the context of the team:
- **`201`**: The member has been successfully added.
- **`202`**: The member needs permission to join the team and an access request
has been generated.
- **`204`**: The member is already on the team.

If the team is provisioned through an identity provider, the member cannot join the
team through Sentry.

Note the permission scopes vary depending on the organization setting `"Open Membership"`
and the type of authorization token. The following table outlines the accepted scopes.
<table style="width: 100%;">
<thead>
    <tr>
    <th style="width: 33%;"></th>
    <th colspan="2" style="text-align: center; font-weight: bold; width: 33%;">Open Membership</th>
    </tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
    <tr>
    <td style="width: 34%;"></td>
    <td style="text-align: center; font-weight: bold; width: 33%;">On</td>
    <td style="text-align: center; font-weight: bold; width: 33%;">Off</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
    <td style="text-align: center; font-weight: bold; vertical-align: middle;"><a
    href="https://docs.sentry.io/account/auth-tokens/#internal-integrations">Internal Integration Token</a></td>
    <td style="text-align: left; width: 33%;">
        <ul style="list-style-type: none; padding-left: 0;">
        <li><strong style="color: #9c5f99;">&bull; org:read</strong></li>
        </ul>
    </td>
    <td style="text-align: left; width: 33%;">
        <ul style="list-style-type: none; padding-left: 0;">
        <li><strong style="color: #9c5f99;">&bull; org:write</strong></li>
        <li><strong style="color: #9c5f99;">&bull; team:write</strong></li>
        </ul>
    </td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
    <td style="text-align: center; font-weight: bold; vertical-align: middle;"><a
    href="https://docs.sentry.io/account/auth-tokens/#user-auth-tokens">User Auth Token</a></td>
    <td style="text-align: left; width: 33%;">
        <ul style="list-style-type: none; padding-left: 0;">
        <li><strong style="color: #9c5f99;">&bull; org:read</strong></li>
        </ul>
    </td>
    <td style="text-align: left; width: 33%;">
        <ul style="list-style-type: none; padding-left: 0;">
        <li><strong style="color: #9c5f99;">&bull; org:read*</strong></li>
        <li><strong style="color: #9c5f99;">&bull; org:write</strong></li>
        <li><strong style="color: #9c5f99;">&bull; org:read +</strong></li>
        <li><strong style="color: #9c5f99;">&nbsp; &nbsp;team:write**</strong></li>
        </ul>
    </td>
    </tr>
</tbody>
</table>


*Organization members are restricted to this scope. When sending a request, it will always
return a 202 and request an invite to the team.


\*\*Team Admins must have both **`org:read`** and **`team:write`** scopes in their user
authorization token to add members to their teams.

<h3 id="add-an-organization-member-to-a-team-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|member_id|path|string|true|The ID of the organization member to add to the team|
|team_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the team the resource belongs to.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": "4502349234123",
  "slug": "ancient-gabelers",

  "avatar": {
    "avatarType": "letter_avatar",
    "avatarUuid": null,
    "avatarUrl": null
  }
}
```

## Delete an Organization Member from a Team

<a id="opIddeleteOrganizationMemberTeam"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/members/string/teams/string/' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/members/{member_id}/teams/{team_id_or_slug}/`

Delete an organization member from a team.

Note the permission scopes vary depending on the type of authorization token. The following
table outlines the accepted scopes.
<table style="width: 100%;">
    <tr style="width: 50%;">
        <td style="width: 50%; text-align: center; font-weight: bold; vertical-align: middle;"><a href="https://docs.sentry.io/api/auth/#auth-tokens">Org Auth Token</a></td>
        <td style="width: 50%; text-align: left;">
            <ul style="list-style-type: none; padding-left: 0;">
                <li><strong style="color: #9c5f99;">&bull; org:write</strong></li>
                <li><strong style="color: #9c5f99;">&bull; org:admin</strong></li>
                <li><strong style="color: #9c5f99;">&bull; team:admin</strong></li>
            </ul>
        </td>
    </tr>
    <tr style="width: 50%;">
        <td style="width: 50%; text-align: center; font-weight: bold; vertical-align: middle;"><a href="https://docs.sentry.io/api/auth/#user-authentication-tokens">User Auth Token</a></td>
        <td style="width: 50%; text-align: left;">
            <ul style="list-style-type: none; padding-left: 0;">
                <li><strong style="color: #9c5f99;">&bull; org:read*</strong></li>
                <li><strong style="color: #9c5f99;">&bull; org:write</strong></li>
                <li><strong style="color: #9c5f99;">&bull; org:admin</strong></li>
                <li><strong style="color: #9c5f99;">&bull; team:admin</strong></li>
                <li><strong style="color: #9c5f99;">&bull; org:read + team:admin**</strong></li>
            </ul>
        </td>
    </tr>
</table>


\***`org:read`** can only be used to remove yourself from the teams you are a member of.


\*\*Team Admins must have both **`org:read`** and **`team:admin`** scopes in their user
authorization token to delete members from their teams.

<h3 id="delete-an-organization-member-from-a-team-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|member_id|path|string|true|The ID of the organization member to delete from the team|
|team_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the team the resource belongs to.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "4502349234123",
  "slug": "ancient-gabelers",
  "name": "Ancient Gabelers",
  "dateCreated": "2023-05-31T19:47:53.621181Z",
  "isMember": false,
  "teamRole": null,
  "flags": {
    "idp:provisioned": false
  },
  "access": [
    "alerts:read",
    "event:write",
    "project:read",
    "team:read",
    "member:read",
    "project:releases",
    "event:read",
    "org:read"
  ],
  "hasAccess": true,
  "isPending": false,
  "memberCount": 3,
  "avatar": {
    "avatarType": "letter_avatar",
    "avatarUuid": null,
    "avatarUrl": null
  }
}
```

<h3 id="delete-an-organization-member-from-a-team-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|403|Forbidden|This team is managed through your organization's identity provider|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<h3 id="delete-an-organization-member-from-a-team-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

## List an Organization's Teams

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationTeams"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/teams/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/teams/`

Returns a list of teams bound to a organization.

<h3 id="list-an-organizations-teams-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|detailed|query|string|false|<br>Specify `"0"` to return team details that do not include projects.<br>|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Limit the number of rows to return in the result. Default and maximum allowed is 100.|
|query|query|string|false|Filter teams by name or slug.|

## Create a New Team

<a id="opIdcreateOrganizationTeam"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/teams/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "slug": "string",
    "name": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/teams/`

Create a new team bound to an organization. Requires at least one of the `name`
or `slug` body params to be set.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "slug": "string",
  "name": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-team-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» slug|body|string \| null|false|Uniquely identifies a team and is used for the interface. If not<br>        provided, it is automatically generated from the name.|
|» name|body|string \| null|false|**Deprecated.** **`[DEPRECATED]`** The name for the team. If not provided, it is<br>        automatically generated from the slug|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": "5151492858",
  "slug": "ancient-gabelers",
  "name": "Ancient Gabelers",
  "dateCreated": "2021-06-12T23:38:54.168307Z",
  "isMember": true,
  "teamRole": "admin",
  "flags": {
    "idp:provisioned": false
  },
  "access": [
    "project:write",

    "project:releases",
    "alerts:write",
    "org:read",
    "team:read",
    "project:admin",
    "project:read",
    "org:integrations",
    "event:read",
    "event:admin",
    "team:write"
  ],
  "hasAccess": true,
  "isPending": false,
  "memberCount": 1,
  "avatar": {
    "avatarType": "letter_avatar",
    "avatarUuid": null,
    "avatarUrl": null
  }
}
```

|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|A team with this slug already exists.|None|

## Update a Team

<a id="opIdupdateTeam"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/teams/string/string/' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "slug": "string",
    "name": "string"
  }'

|body|body|object|true|none|
|» slug|body|string|true|Uniquely identifies a team. This is must be available.|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the team.|

## Delete a Team

<a id="opIddeleteTeam"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/teams/string/string/' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /api/0/teams/{organization_id_or_slug}/{team_id_or_slug}/`

Schedules a team for deletion.

**Note:** Deletion happens asynchronously and therefore is not
immediate. Teams will have their slug released while waiting for deletion.

<h3 id="delete-a-team-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|team_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the team the resource belongs to.|

<h3 id="delete-a-team-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|No Content|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
auth_token
</aside>

## List a Team's Members

<a id="opIdlistTeamMembers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/teams/string/string/members/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/teams/{organization_id_or_slug}/{team_id_or_slug}/members/`

List all members on a team.

The response will not include members with pending invites.

|team_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the team the resource belongs to.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|

  }'

`PUT /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/`

Update various attributes and configurable settings for the given organization.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "slug": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "isEarlyAdopter": true,
  "hideAiFeatures": true,
  "defaultRole": "member",
  "openMembership": true,
  "eventsMemberAdmin": true,
  "alertsMemberWrite": true,
  "attachmentsRole": "member",
  "debugFilesRole": "member",
  "hasGranularReplayPermissions": true,
  "replayAccessMembers": [
    0
  ],
  "avatarType": "letter_avatar",
  "avatar": "string",
  "require2FA": true,
  "allowSharedIssues": true,
  "enhancedPrivacy": true,
  "scrapeJavaScript": true,
  "storeCrashReports": 0,
  "allowJoinRequests": true,
  "dataScrubber": true,
  "dataScrubberDefaults": true,
  "sensitiveFields": [
    "string"
  ],
  "safeFields": [
    "string"
  ],
  "scrubIPAddresses": true,
  "relayPiiConfig": "string",
  "trustedRelays": [
    {
      "property1": null,
      "property2": null
    }

  "relayDsnEndpoint": "string",
  "issueAlertsThreadFlag": true,
  "metricAlertsThreadFlag": true,
  "cancelDeletion": true,
  "apdexThreshold": 0
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» slug|body|string|false|The new slug for the organization, which needs to be unique.|
|» name|body|string|false|The new name for the organization.|
|» isEarlyAdopter|body|boolean|false|Specify `true` to opt-in to new features before they're released to the public.|
|» hideAiFeatures|body|boolean|false|Specify `true` to hide AI features from the organization.|
|» defaultRole|body|string|false|The default role new members will receive.<br><br>* `member` - Member<br>* `admin` - Admin<br>* `manager` - Manager<br>* `owner` - Owner|
|» openMembership|body|boolean|false|Specify `true` to allow organization members to freely join any team.|
|» eventsMemberAdmin|body|boolean|false|Specify `true` to allow members to delete events (including the delete & discard action) by granting them the `event:admin` scope.|
|» alertsMemberWrite|body|boolean|false|Specify `true` to allow members to create, edit, and delete alert rules by granting them the `alerts:write` scope.|
|» attachmentsRole|body|string|false|The role required to download event attachments, such as native crash reports or log files.<br><br>* `member` - Member<br>* `admin` - Admin<br>* `manager` - Manager<br>* `owner` - Owner|
|» debugFilesRole|body|string|false|The role required to download debug information files, ProGuard mappings and source maps.<br><br>* `member` - Member<br>* `admin` - Admin<br>* `manager` - Manager<br>* `owner` - Owner|
|» hasGranularReplayPermissions|body|boolean|false|Specify `true` to enable granular replay permissions, allowing per-member access control for replay data.|
|» replayAccessMembers|body|[integer]|false|A list of user IDs who have permission to access replay data. Requires the hasGranularReplayPermissions flag to be true to be enforced.|
|» avatarType|body|string|false|The type of display picture for the organization.<br><br>* `letter_avatar` - Use initials<br>* `upload` - Upload an image|
|» avatar|body|string|false|The image to upload as the organization avatar, in base64. Required if `avatarType` is `upload`.|
|» require2FA|body|boolean|false|Specify `true` to require and enforce two-factor authentication for all members.|
|» allowSharedIssues|body|boolean|false|Specify `true` to allow sharing of limited details on issues to anonymous users.|
|» enhancedPrivacy|body|boolean|false|Specify `true` to enable enhanced privacy controls to limit personally identifiable information (PII) as well as source code in things like notifications.|
|» scrapeJavaScript|body|boolean|false|Specify `true` to allow Sentry to scrape missing JavaScript source context when possible.|
|» storeCrashReports|body|integer|false|How many native crash reports (such as Minidumps for improved processing and download in issue details) to store per issue.<br><br>* `0` - Disabled<br>* `1` - 1 per issue<br>* `5` - 5 per issue<br>* `10` - 10 per issue<br>* `20` - 20 per issue<br>* `50` - 50 per issue<br>* `100` - 100 per issue<br>* `-1` - Unlimited|
|» allowJoinRequests|body|boolean|false|Specify `true` to allow users to request to join your organization.|
|» dataScrubber|body|boolean|false|Specify `true` to require server-side data scrubbing for all projects.|
|» dataScrubberDefaults|body|boolean|false|Specify `true` to apply the default scrubbers to prevent things like passwords and credit cards from being stored for all projects.|
|» sensitiveFields|body|[string]|false|A list of additional global field names to match against when scrubbing data for all projects.|
|» safeFields|body|[string]|false|A list of global field names which data scrubbers should ignore.|
|» scrubIPAddresses|body|boolean|false|Specify `true` to prevent IP addresses from being stored for new events on all projects.|
|» relayPiiConfig|body|string|false|Advanced data scrubbing rules that can be configured for each project as a JSON string. The new rules will only apply to new incoming events. For more details on advanced data scrubbing, see our [full documentation](/security-legal-pii/scrubbing/advanced-datascrubbing/).<br><br>> Warning: Calling this endpoint with this field fully overwrites the advanced data scrubbing rules.<br><br>Below is an example of a payload for a set of advanced data scrubbing rules for masking credit card numbers from the log message (equivalent to `[Mask] [Credit card numbers] from [$message]` in the Sentry app) and removing a specific key called `foo` (equivalent to `[Remove] [Anything] from [extra.foo]` in the Sentry app):<br>```json<br>{<br>    relayPiiConfig: "{\"rules":{\"0\":{\"type\":\"creditcard\",\"redaction\":{\"method\":\"mask\"}},\"1\":{\"type\":\"anything\",\"redaction\":{\"method\":\"remove\"}}},\"applications\":{\"$message\":[\"0\"],\"extra.foo\":[\"1\"]}}"<br>}<br>```<br>        |
|» trustedRelays|body|[object]|false|A list of local Relays (the name, public key, and description as a JSON) registered for the organization. This feature is only available for organizations on the Business and Enterprise plans. Read more about Relay [here](/product/relay/).<br><br>                                          Below is an example of a list containing a single local Relay registered for the organization:<br>                                          ```json<br>                                          {<br>                                            trustedRelays: [<br>                                                {<br>                                                    name: "my-relay",<br>                                                    publicKey: "eiwr9fdruw4erfh892qy4493reyf89ur34wefd90h",<br>                                                    description: "Configuration for my-relay."<br>                                                }<br>                                            ]<br>                                          }<br>                                          ```<br>                                          |
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» relayDsnEndpoint|body|string \| null|false|A Relay base URL to use when displaying Client Key DSNs for this organization.|
|» issueAlertsThreadFlag|body|boolean|false|Specify `true` to allow the Sentry Slack integration to post replies in threads for an Issue Alert notification. Requires a Slack integration.|
|» metricAlertsThreadFlag|body|boolean|false|Specify `true` to allow the Sentry Slack integration to post replies in threads for a Metric Alert notification. Requires a Slack integration.|
|» cancelDeletion|body|boolean|false|Specify `true` to restore an organization that is pending deletion.|
|» apdexThreshold|body|integer|false|Deprecated. Response-time threshold in milliseconds previously used to compute Apdex.|

## Retrieve Chunk Upload Options

<a id="opIdgetOrganizationChunkUploadOptions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/chunk-upload/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/chunk-upload/`

**Experimental:** This API is under active development and may change.

Return the URL and limits to use when uploading file chunks, such as the chunk size,
the number of chunks per request, and the supported compression.

<h3 id="retrieve-chunk-upload-options-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "url": "string",
  "chunkSize": 0,
  "chunksPerRequest": 0,
  "maxFileSize": 0,
  "maxRequestSize": 0,
  "concurrency": 0,
  "hashAlgorithm": "string",
  "compression": [
    "string"
  ],
  "accept": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-chunk-upload-options-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<h3 id="retrieve-chunk-upload-options-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|url|string|true|none|none|
|chunkSize|integer|true|none|none|
|chunksPerRequest|integer|true|none|none|
|maxFileSize|integer|true|none|none|
|maxRequestSize|integer|true|none|none|

|compression|[string]|true|none|none|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

## Upload File Chunks

<a id="opIduploadOrganizationChunks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/chunk-upload/' \
  -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'file=["http://example.com"]'
```

`POST /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/chunk-upload/`

**Experimental:** This API is under active development and may change.

Upload file chunks so they can be assembled into debug information files or artifact
bundles. Send requests to the URL from the chunk upload options, which uses the
region-specific domain (for example `us.sentry.io` or `de.sentry.io`).

Chunks may be compressed with one of the codecs listed in the options. Select it with
the `Content-Encoding` request header. Resending a chunk is safe: chunks are stored
by checksum, so an identical upload changes nothing.

> Body parameter

```yaml
file:
  - "http://example.com"
```

<h3 id="upload-file-chunks-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» file|body|[string(uri)]|true|The chunks to upload. Name each part after the SHA-1 checksum of its uncompressed content. Repeat the field for each chunk, up to `chunksPerRequest` per request.|

<h3 id="upload-file-chunks-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success|None|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
auth_token
</aside>

## List an Organization's Members

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationMembers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/members/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/members/`

List all organization members.

Response includes pending invites that are approved by organization owners or managers but waiting to be accepted by the invitee.

<h3 id="list-an-organizations-members-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|query|query|string|false|Limit results to members matching the given query. `id, `user.id`, ... are supported prefixes match on: `id`, `user.id`, `email`, `role`, `scope`, `isInvited`, `ssoLinked`, `has2fa`, `hasExternalUsers`. For example, `query=user.id:1234`. An unrecognized field returns no results.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|

## Add a Member to an Organization

<a id="opIdaddOrganizationMember"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/members/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "role": "member",
    "orgRole": "member",
    "teams": [
      null
    ],
    "teamRoles": [
      {
        "property1": null,
        "property2": null
      }
    ],
    "sendInvite": true,
    "reinvite": true,
    "regenerate": true
  }'
```

`POST /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/members/`

Add or invite a member to an organization.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email": "user@example.com",
  "role": "member",
  "orgRole": "member",
  "teams": [
    null
  ],
  "teamRoles": [
    {
      "property1": null,
      "property2": null
    }
  ],
  "sendInvite": true,
  "reinvite": true,
  "regenerate": true
}
```

<h3 id="add-a-member-to-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» email|body|string(email)|true|The email address to send the invitation to.|
|» role|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated, use `orgRole`. The organization-level role to assign.<br><br>* `member` - Member<br>* `admin` - Admin<br>* `manager` - Manager<br>* `owner` - Owner|
|» orgRole|body|string|false|The organization-level role of the new member. Roles include:<br><br>* `billing` - Can manage payment and compliance details.<br>* `member` - Can view and act on events, as well as view most other data within the organization.<br>* `manager` - Has full management access to all teams and projects. Can also manage<br>        the organization's membership.<br>* `owner` - Has unrestricted access to the organization, its data, and its<br>        settings. Can add, modify, and delete projects and members, as well as<br>        make billing and plan changes.<br>* `admin` - Can edit global integrations, manage projects, and add/remove teams.<br>        They automatically assume the Team Admin role for teams they join.<br>        Note: This role can no longer be assigned in Business and Enterprise plans. Use `TeamRoles` instead.<br>        |
|» teams|body|[object]|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated, use `teamRoles`. Slugs of teams to add the member to.|
|» teamRoles|body|[object]|false|The team and team-roles assigned to the member. Team roles can be either:<br>        - `contributor` - Can view and act on issues. Depending on organization settings, they can also add team members.<br>        - `admin` - Has full management access to their team's membership and projects.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» sendInvite|body|boolean|false|Whether or not to send an invite notification through email. Defaults to True.|
|» reinvite|body|boolean|false|Whether or not to re-invite a user who has already been invited to the organization. Defaults to True.|
|» regenerate|body|boolean|false|Reissue the invite token, invalidating any previously sent invite link.|

#### Enumerated Values

|» role|admin|
|» role|manager|
|» role|owner|
|» orgRole|billing|
|» orgRole|member|
|» orgRole|manager|
|» orgRole|owner|
|» orgRole|admin|

curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/members/string/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/members/{member_id}/`

Retrieve an organization member's details.

Response will be a pending invite if it has been approved by organization owners or managers but is waiting to be accepted by the invitee.

<h3 id="retrieve-an-organization-member-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|member_id|path|string|true|The ID of the organization member.|

## Update an Organization Member's Roles

<a id="opIdupdateOrganizationMember"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/members/string/' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "orgRole": "billing",
    "teamRoles": [
      {
        "property1": null,
        "property2": null
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/members/{member_id}/`

Update a member's [organization-level](https://docs.sentry.io/organization/membership/#organization-level-roles) and [team-level](https://docs.sentry.io/organization/membership/#team-level-roles) roles.

Note that for changing organization-roles, this endpoint is restricted to
[user auth tokens](https://docs.sentry.io/account/auth-tokens/#user-auth-tokens).
Additionally, both the original and desired organization role must have
the same or lower permissions than the role of the organization user making the request

For example, an organization Manager may change someone's role from
Member to Manager, but not to Owner.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "orgRole": "billing",
  "teamRoles": [
    {
      "property1": null,
      "property2": null
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-organization-members-roles-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|member_id|path|string|true|The ID of the member to update.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» orgRole|body|string|false|The organization role of the member. The options are:<br><br>* `billing` - Can manage payment and compliance details.<br>* `member` - Can view and act on events, as well as view most other data within the organization.<br>* `manager` - Has full management access to all teams and projects. Can also manage<br>        the organization's membership.<br>* `owner` - Has unrestricted access to the organization, its data, and its<br>        settings. Can add, modify, and delete projects and members, as well as<br>        make billing and plan changes.<br>* `admin` - Can edit global integrations, manage projects, and add/remove teams.<br>        They automatically assume the Team Admin role for teams they join.<br>        Note: This role can no longer be assigned in Business and Enterprise plans. Use `TeamRoles` instead.<br>        |
|» teamRoles|body|[object]|false|<br>Configures the team role of the member. The two roles are:<br>- `contributor` - Can view and act on issues. Depending on organization settings, they can also add team members.<br>- `admin` - Has full management access to their team's membership and projects.<br>```json<br>{<br>    "teamRoles": [<br>        {<br>            "teamSlug": "ancient-gabelers",<br>            "role": "admin"<br>        },<br>        {<br>            "teamSlug": "powerful-abolitionist",<br>            "role": "contributor"<br>        }<br>    ]<br>}<br>```<br>|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» orgRole|billing|
|» orgRole|member|
|» orgRole|manager|
|» orgRole|owner|
|» orgRole|admin|

## List an Organization's Client Keys

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationProjectKeys"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/project-keys/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/project-keys/`

Return a list of client keys (DSNs) for all projects in an organization.

This paginated endpoint lists client keys across all projects in an organization. Each key includes the project ID
to identify which project it belongs to.

Query Parameters:
- team: Filter by team slug or ID to get keys only for that team's projects
- status: Filter by 'active' or 'inactive' to get keys with specific status

<h3 id="list-an-organizations-client-keys-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|
|team|query|string|false|Filter keys by team slug or ID. If provided, only keys for projects belonging to this team will be returned.|
|status|query|string|false|Filter keys by status. Options are 'active' or 'inactive'.<br><br>* `active`<br>* `inactive`|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|active|
|status|inactive|

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/repos/`

<h3 id="list-an-organizations-repositories-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|expand|query|[string]|false|Optional repository fields to expand, such as `settings`.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The maximum number of repositories to return per page (1–100).|

## Retrieve an Organization's Events Count by Project

<a id="opIdgetOrganizationStatsSummary"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/stats-summary/?field=sum(quantity)' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/stats-summary/`

Query summarized event counts by project for your Organization. Also see https://docs.sentry.io/api/organizations/retrieve-event-counts-for-an-organization-v2/ for reference.

<h3 id="retrieve-an-organizations-events-count-by-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|field|query|string|true|the `sum(quantity)` field is bytes for attachments, and all others the 'event' count for those types of events.<br><br>`sum(times_seen)` sums the number of times an event has been seen. For 'normal' event types, this will be equal to `sum(quantity)` for now. For sessions, quantity will sum the total number of events seen in a session, while `times_seen` will be the unique number of sessions. and for attachments, `times_seen` will be the total number of attachments, while quantity will be the total sum of attachment bytes.<br><br>* `sum(quantity)`<br>* `sum(times_seen)`|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|This defines the range of the time series, relative to now. The range is given in a `<number><unit>` format. For example `1d` for a one day range. Possible units are `m` for minutes, `h` for hours, `d` for days and `w` for weeks. You must either provide a `statsPeriod`, or a `start` and `end`.|
|interval|query|string|false|This is the resolution of the time series, given in the same format as `statsPeriod`. The default resolution is `1h` and the minimum resolution is currently restricted to `1h` as well. Intervals larger than `1d` are not supported, and the interval has to cleanly divide one day.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|This defines the start of the time series range as an explicit datetime, either in UTC ISO8601 or epoch seconds. Use along with `end` instead of `statsPeriod`.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|This defines the inclusive end of the time series range as an explicit datetime, either in UTC ISO8601 or epoch seconds. Use along with `start` instead of `statsPeriod`.|
|project|query|[object]|false|The ID of the projects to filter by.|
|category|query|string|false|If filtering by attachments, you cannot filter by any other category due to quantity values becoming nonsensical (combining bytes and event counts).<br><br>If filtering by `error`, it will automatically add `default` and `security` as we currently roll those two categories into `error` for displaying.<br><br>* `error`<br>* `transaction`<br>* `attachment`<br>* `replays`<br>* `profiles`|
|outcome|query|string|false|See https://docs.sentry.io/product/stats/ for more information on outcome statuses.<br><br>* `accepted`<br>* `filtered`<br>* `rate_limited`<br>* `invalid`<br>* `abuse`<br>* `client_discard`<br>* `cardinality_limited`|
|reason|query|string|false|The reason field will contain why an event was filtered/dropped.|
|download|query|boolean|false|Download the API response in as a csv file|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|field|sum(quantity)|
|field|sum(times_seen)|
|category|error|
|category|transaction|
|category|attachment|
|category|replays|
|category|profiles|
|outcome|accepted|
|outcome|filtered|
|outcome|rate_limited|
|outcome|invalid|
|outcome|abuse|
|outcome|client_discard|
|outcome|cardinality_limited|

## Retrieve Event Counts for an Organization (v2)

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationStatsV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/stats_v2/?groupBy=outcome&field=sum(quantity)' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/stats_v2/`

Query event counts for your Organization.
Select a field, define a date range, and group or filter by columns.

<h3 id="retrieve-event-counts-for-an-organization-v2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|groupBy|query|[string]|true|can pass multiple groupBy parameters to group by multiple, e.g. `groupBy=project&groupBy=outcome` to group by multiple dimensions. Note that grouping by project can cause missing rows if the number of projects / interval is large. If you have a large number of projects, we recommend filtering and querying by them individually.Also note that grouping by projects does not currently support timeseries interval responses and will instead be a sum of the projectover the entire period specified.|
|field|query|string|true|the `sum(quantity)` field is bytes for attachments, and all others the 'event' count for those types of events.<br><br>`sum(times_seen)` sums the number of times an event has been seen. For 'normal' event types, this will be equal to `sum(quantity)` for now. For sessions, quantity will sum the total number of events seen in a session, while `times_seen` will be the unique number of sessions. and for attachments, `times_seen` will be the total number of attachments, while quantity will be the total sum of attachment bytes.<br><br>* `sum(quantity)`<br>* `sum(times_seen)`|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|This defines the range of the time series, relative to now. The range is given in a `<number><unit>` format. For example `1d` for a one day range. Possible units are `m` for minutes, `h` for hours, `d` for days and `w` for weeks. You must either provide a `statsPeriod`, or a `start` and `end`.|
|interval|query|string|false|This is the resolution of the time series, given in the same format as `statsPeriod`. The default resolution is `1h` and the minimum resolution is currently restricted to `1h` as well. Intervals larger than `1d` are not supported, and the interval has to cleanly divide one day.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|This defines the start of the time series range as an explicit datetime, either in UTC ISO8601 or epoch seconds. Use along with `end` instead of `statsPeriod`.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|This defines the inclusive end of the time series range as an explicit datetime, either in UTC ISO8601 or epoch seconds. Use along with `start` instead of `statsPeriod`.|
|project|query|[object]|false|The ID of the projects to filter by.<br><br>Use `-1` to include all accessible projects.|
|category|query|string|false|Filter by data category. Each category represents a different type of data:<br><br>- `error`: Error events (includes `default` and `security` categories)<br>- `transaction`: Transaction events<br>- `attachment`: File attachments (note: cannot be combined with other categories since quantity represents bytes)<br>- `replay`: Session replay events<br>- `profile`: Performance profiles<br>- `profile_duration`: Profile duration data (note: cannot be combined with other categories since quantity represents milliseconds)<br>- `profile_duration_ui`: Profile duration (UI) data (note: cannot be combined with other categories since quantity represents milliseconds)<br>- `profile_chunk`: Profile chunk data<br>- `profile_chunk_ui`: Profile chunk (UI) data<br>- `monitor`: Cron monitor events<br><br>* `error`<br>* `transaction`<br>* `attachment`<br>* `replay`<br>* `profile`<br>* `profile_duration`<br>* `profile_duration_ui`<br>* `profile_chunk`<br>* `profile_chunk_ui`<br>* `monitor`|
|outcome|query|string|false|See https://docs.sentry.io/product/stats/ for more information on outcome statuses.<br><br>* `accepted`<br>* `filtered`<br>* `rate_limited`<br>* `invalid`<br>* `abuse`<br>* `client_discard`<br>* `cardinality_limited`|
|reason|query|string|false|The reason field will contain why an event was filtered/dropped.|

## Create a Project for an Organization

<a id="opIdcreateOrganizationProject"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/projects/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "slug": "string",
    "platform": "string",
    "default_rules": true
  }'
```

`POST /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/projects/`

Create a new project for an organization. A personal team (`team-{username}`) is automatically created for the caller with Team Admin role, and the project is bound to it. If the org has member project creation disabled (`disable_member_project_creation`), `org:write` scope is required.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "slug": "string",
  "platform": "string",
  "default_rules": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-project-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name for the project.|
|» slug|body|string \| null|false|Uniquely identifies a project and is used for the interface.<br>        If not provided, it is automatically generated from the name.|
|» platform|body|string \| null|false|The platform for the project.|
|» default_rules|body|boolean|false|<br>Defaults to true where the behavior is to alert the user on every new<br>issue. Setting this to false will turn this off and the user must create<br>their own alerts to be notified of new issues.<br>        |

`PUT /api/0/projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/`

Update various attributes and configurable settings for the given project.

Note that solely having the **`project:read`** scope restricts updatable settings to
`isBookmarked`, `autofixAutomationTuning`, `seerScannerAutomation`,
`preprodSizeStatusChecksEnabled`, `preprodSizeStatusChecksRules`,
`preprodSizePrCommentsEnabled`, `preprodSizePrCommentsRules`,
`preprodSizeEnabledQuery`, `preprodDistributionEnabledQuery`,
`preprodSizeEnabledByCustomer`, `preprodDistributionEnabledByCustomer`,
and `preprodDistributionPrCommentsEnabledByCustomer`.

<h3 id="update-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» digestsMinDelay|body|integer|true|Minimum time in seconds to wait before sending an issue digest email.|
|» digestsMaxDelay|body|integer|true|Maximum time in seconds to wait before sending an issue digest email.|
|» securityToken|body|string|true|Token sent with security reports (CSP, Expect-CT, HPKP) so Sentry can verify their origin.|
|» securityTokenHeader|body|string|true|Name of the header carrying the security token on inbound security reports.|
|» isBookmarked|body|boolean|false|Enables starring the project within the projects tab. Can be updated with **`project:read`** permission.|
|» autofixAutomationTuning|body|string|false|How aggressively Seer runs Autofix on new issues. Can be updated with **`project:read`** permission.<br><br>* `off`<br>* `super_low`<br>* `low`<br>* `medium`<br>* `high`<br>* `always`|
|» seerScannerAutomation|body|boolean|false|Let Seer scan new issues automatically. Can be updated with **`project:read`** permission.|
|» preprodSizeStatusChecksEnabled|body|boolean|false|Enable preprod size status checks. Can be updated with **`project:read`** permission.|
|» preprodSizeStatusChecksRules|body|object|false|Rules controlling when preprod size status checks fail. Can be updated with **`project:read`** permission.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» preprodSizePrCommentsEnabled|body|boolean|false|Enable preprod size PR comments. Can be updated with **`project:read`** permission.|
|» preprodSizePrCommentsRules|body|object|false|Rules controlling which preprod size changes are posted as PR comments. Can be updated with **`project:read`** permission.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» preprodSnapshotStatusChecksEnabled|body|boolean|false|Enable preprod snapshot status checks.|
|» preprodSnapshotStatusChecksFailOnAdded|body|boolean|false|Fail the preprod snapshot status check when snapshots are added.|
|» preprodSnapshotStatusChecksFailOnRemoved|body|boolean|false|Fail the preprod snapshot status check when snapshots are removed.|
|» preprodSnapshotStatusChecksFailOnChanged|body|boolean|false|Fail the preprod snapshot status check when snapshots change.|
|» preprodSnapshotStatusChecksFailOnRenamed|body|boolean|false|Fail the preprod snapshot status check when snapshots are renamed.|
|» preprodSizeEnabledByCustomer|body|boolean \| null|false|Enable preprod size analysis. Can be updated with **`project:read`** permission.|
|» preprodDistributionEnabledByCustomer|body|boolean \| null|false|Enable preprod build distribution. Can be updated with **`project:read`** permission.|
|» preprodDistributionPrCommentsEnabledByCustomer|body|boolean \| null|false|Post preprod distribution updates as PR comments. Can be updated with **`project:read`** permission.|
|» preprodSnapshotPrCommentsEnabled|body|boolean \| null|false|Post preprod snapshot changes as PR comments.|
|» preprodSnapshotPrCommentsPostOnAdded|body|boolean \| null|false|Include added snapshots in preprod snapshot PR comments.|
|» preprodSnapshotPrCommentsPostOnRemoved|body|boolean \| null|false|Include removed snapshots in preprod snapshot PR comments.|
|» preprodSnapshotPrCommentsPostOnChanged|body|boolean \| null|false|Include changed snapshots in preprod snapshot PR comments.|
|» preprodSnapshotPrCommentsPostOnRenamed|body|boolean \| null|false|Include renamed snapshots in preprod snapshot PR comments.|
|» preprodSizeEnabledQuery|body|string \| null|false|Query selecting which preprod builds are size-analyzed. Can be updated with **`project:read`** permission.|
|» preprodDistributionEnabledQuery|body|string \| null|false|Query selecting which preprod builds are distributed. Can be updated with **`project:read`** permission.|
|» name|body|string|false|The name for the project|
|» slug|body|string|false|Uniquely identifies a project and is used for the interface.|
|» platform|body|string \| null|false|The platform for the project|
|» subjectPrefix|body|string|false|Custom prefix for emails from this project.|
|» subjectTemplate|body|string|false|The email subject to use (excluding the prefix) for individual alerts. Here are the list of variables you can use:<br>- `$title`<br>- `$shortID`<br>- `$projectID`<br>- `$orgID`<br>- `${tag:key}` - such as `${tag:environment}` or `${tag:release}`.|
|» resolveAge|body|integer \| null|false|Automatically resolve an issue if it hasn't been seen for this many hours. Set to `0` to disable auto-resolve.|
|» highlightContext|body|object|false|A JSON mapping of context types to lists of strings for their keys.<br>E.g. `{'user': ['id', 'email']}`|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» highlightTags|body|[string]|false|A list of strings with tag keys to highlight on this project's issues.<br>E.g. `['release', 'environment']`|
|» verifySSL|body|boolean|false|Verify SSL certificates when delivering outbound webhooks and service hooks.|
|» defaultEnvironment|body|string \| null|false|Environment selected by default when viewing this project.|
|» dataScrubber|body|boolean|false|Remove known sensitive values from events before storing them.|
|» dataScrubberDefaults|body|boolean|false|Also scrub Sentry's built-in list of sensitive field names.|
|» sensitiveFields|body|[string]|false|Additional field names to scrub from events, beyond the defaults.|
|» safeFields|body|[string]|false|Field names to exempt from scrubbing, including the built-in defaults.|
|» storeCrashReports|body|integer \| null|false|Number of native crash report files to store per issue. Use `-1` for unlimited or `0` to store none.|
|» relayPiiConfig|body|string \| null|false|Advanced data scrubbing rules, as a JSON string, applied before events are stored.|
|» builtinSymbolSources|body|[string]|false|Identifiers of Sentry-hosted symbol sources to use when symbolicating events.|
|» symbolSources|body|string \| null|false|Custom symbol sources, as a JSON string, to use when symbolicating events.|
|» enableNativeSourceServerMapping|body|boolean|false|Apply source server (srcsrv) information from native debug files to symbolicated frames.|
|» scrubIPAddresses|body|boolean|false|Discard client IP addresses rather than storing them on events.|
|» groupingConfig|body|string \| null|false|Identifier of the grouping algorithm used to assign events to issues.|
|» groupingEnhancements|body|string \| null|false|Grouping enhancement rules, as a newline-delimited config string, adjusting which stack frames contribute to an issue.|
|» fingerprintingRules|body|string \| null|false|Fingerprinting rules, as a newline-delimited config string, controlling how events are grouped into issues.|
|» secondaryGroupingConfig|body|string \| null|false|Grouping algorithm run alongside the primary one during a grouping migration.|
|» secondaryGroupingExpiry|body|integer \| null|false|Unix timestamp after which the secondary grouping algorithm stops running.|
|» scrapeJavaScript|body|boolean|false|Allow Sentry to fetch source files and source maps from your servers.|
|» enableAutoReleaseCreation|body|boolean|false|Automatically create releases from ingested events. When disabled, releases must be created manually (e.g. via the Sentry CLI).|
|» allowedDomains|body|[string]|false|Origins permitted to send events to this project. Use `*` to allow any.|
|» copy_from_project|body|integer|false|ID of a project whose settings, teams, and keys should be copied into this one.|
|» targetSampleRate|body|number(double)|false|Target proportion of transactions to retain, from `0` to `1`. Requires manual dynamic sampling mode.|
|» dynamicSamplingBiases|body|[object]|false|Per-bias toggles adjusting which transactions dynamic sampling favors retaining.|
|» » id|body|string|true|* `boostEnvironments`<br>* `boostKeyTransactions`<br>* `boostLatestRelease`<br>* `boostLowVolumeTransactions`<br>* `boostReplayId`<br>* `ignoreHealthChecks`<br>* `minimumSampleRate`<br>* `recalibrationRule`|
|» » active|body|boolean|false|none|
|» tempestFetchScreenshots|body|boolean|false|Fetch screenshots attached to console crash reports. Requires the Tempest feature.|
|» scmSourceContextEnabled|body|boolean|false|Enable on-demand source context fetching from SCM integrations for stack traces.|
|» debugFilesRole|body|string \| null|false|The role required to download debug information files, ProGuard mappings and source maps. If not set, inherits from organization setting.<br><br>* `member` - Member<br>* `admin` - Admin<br>* `manager` - Manager<br>* `owner` - Owner|

## Delete a Project

<a id="opIddeleteProject"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/projects/string/string/' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /api/0/projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/`

Schedules a project for deletion.

Deletion happens asynchronously and therefore is not immediate. However once deletion has
begun the state of a project changes and will be hidden from most public views.

<h3 id="delete-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|

<h3 id="delete-a-project-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|No Content|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
auth_token
</aside>

`GET /api/0/projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/codeowners/`

## Create a CODEOWNERS Configuration for a Project

<a id="opIdcreateProjectCodeOwners"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/projects/string/string/codeowners/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "raw": "src/* user@example.com",
    "codeMappingId": "7"
  }'
```

`POST /api/0/projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/codeowners/`

Create a CODEOWNERS configuration for a project.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "raw": "src/* user@example.com",
  "codeMappingId": "7"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-codeowners-configuration-for-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» raw|body|string|true|The raw contents of the CODEOWNERS file.|
|» codeMappingId|body|string|true|The ID of the code mapping used to translate repository paths to stack trace paths.|

> 201 Response

  "id": "42",
  "raw": "src/* user@example.com",

In addition, `error` accepts `error_type`, `error_message` and `geo_country_code`, `log` accepts `log_message`, and `metric` accepts `metric_name`. `span` and `all` accept no other types.<br><br>* `error_type`<br>* `error_message`<br>* `log_message`<br>* `metric_name`<br>* `release`<br>* `ip_address`<br>* `geo_country_code`|

|» » value|[string]|true|none|The values the field is compared to. The condition matches when any value matches, so multiple values act as OR; a negated operator matches when none does. A version comparison takes one release with a version such as `1.2.0` or `myapp@1.2.0`. A comparison with a package only applies to releases of that package.|

<h3 id="retrieve-a-custom-inbound-filter-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|read-only|The ID of the filter.|
|dataType|string|true|none|The data the filter matches against. `all` is the catch-all: it filters every data type Sentry ingests, including ones added later, and accepts only the conditions that every data type carries a field for.<br><br>* `all`<br>* `error`<br>* `log`<br>* `metric`<br>* `span`|
|conditions|[object]|true|none|Conditions are combined with AND: an event must match every condition to be filtered out. There is no OR between conditions, so e.g. two release conditions can express a range (`gte 2.0` and `lt 4.0`). To broaden matching, widen a condition's values or add separate filters.|
|» type|string|true|none|The field the condition matches against. Every `dataType` accepts `release` and `ip_address`. In addition, `error` accepts `error_type`, `error_message` and `geo_country_code`, `log` accepts `log_message`, and `metric` accepts `metric_name`. `span` and `all` accept no other types.<br><br>* `error_type`<br>* `error_message`<br>* `log_message`<br>* `metric_name`<br>* `release`<br>* `ip_address`<br>* `geo_country_code`|
|» operator|string|false|none|How the field compares to `value`. `glob` matches the field against each value as a glob pattern. `equals`, `starts_with`, `contains` and `ends_with` match the field against each value case-insensitively, with every character read literally; `does_not_start_with`, `does_not_contain` and `does_not_end_with` match when no value does. `cidr` matches `ip_address` against each value as an address or a CIDR range, and `not_cidr` matches when no value does. `gt`, `gte`, `lt` and `lte` compare one value as a version and only apply to `release`.<br><br>* `glob`<br>* `equals`<br>* `starts_with`<br>* `contains`<br>* `ends_with`<br>* `does_not_start_with`<br>* `does_not_contain`<br>* `does_not_end_with`<br>* `cidr`<br>* `not_cidr`<br>* `gt`<br>* `gte`<br>* `lt`<br>* `lte`|
|» value|[string]|true|none|The values the field is compared to. The condition matches when any value matches, so multiple values act as OR; a negated operator matches when none does. A version comparison takes one release with a version such as `1.2.0` or `myapp@1.2.0`. A comparison with a package only applies to releases of that package.|
|dateCreated|string(date-time)|true|read-only|When the filter was created.|
|dateUpdated|string(date-time)|true|read-only|When the filter was last changed.|
|legacyFilter|string \| null|true|read-only|Set on a filter that holds one of the filter lists of the project settings, to the id its outcomes are reported under. Such a filter keeps its data type and its one condition: only the name, the active flag and the condition values can change, and deleting it empties the list.|
|name|string \| null|false|none|A human-readable label for the filter.|
|active|boolean|false|none|Whether the filter drops matching data. An inactive filter is kept but ignored.|

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

## Assemble Debug Information Files

<a id="opIdassembleProjectDebugFiles"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/projects/string/string/files/difs/assemble/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "property1": {
      "name": "string",
      "chunks": [
        "string"
      ],
      "debug_id": "string"
    },
    "property2": {
      "name": "string",
      "chunks": [
        "string"
      ],
      "debug_id": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/0/projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/files/difs/assemble/`

**Experimental:** This API is under active development and may change.

Assemble previously uploaded chunks into debug information files.

The response reports each file's `state`, keyed by the same checksums. If chunks are
missing, upload them and send the request again. Repeat the request to poll until the
state is `ok` or `error`. Resending an identical request is safe: a file that is
already assembling or assembled reports its state instead of starting a new job.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "property1": {
    "name": "string",
    "chunks": [
      "string"
    ],
    "debug_id": "string"
  },
  "property2": {
    "name": "string",
    "chunks": [
      "string"
    ],
    "debug_id": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="assemble-debug-information-files-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» » name|body|string|true|The file name. A ProGuard mapping without `debug_id` can carry it in the name, as in `/proguard/mapping-<uuid>.txt`.|
|» » chunks|body|[string]|true|The SHA-1 checksums of the file's chunks, in order. Upload missing chunks with the chunk upload endpoint. Send an empty list to poll the file's state.|
|» » debug_id|body|string|false|The debug ID to store the file under, overriding the one read from the file.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "property1": {
    "state": "string",
    "missingChunks": [
      "string"
    ],
    "detail": "string",
    "dif": {
      "id": "string",
      "uuid": "string",
      "debugId": "string",
      "codeId": "string",
      "cpuName": "string",
      "objectName": "string",
      "symbolType": "string",
      "headers": {
        "property1": "string",
        "property2": "string"
      },
      "size": 0,
      "sha1": "string",
      "dateCreated": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "data": {
        "property1": null,
        "property2": null
      }
    }
  },
  "property2": {
    "state": "string",
    "missingChunks": [
      "string"
    ],
    "detail": "string",
    "dif": {
      "id": "string",
      "uuid": "string",
      "debugId": "string",
      "codeId": "string",
      "cpuName": "string",
      "objectName": "string",
      "symbolType": "string",
      "headers": {
        "property1": "string",
        "property2": "string"
      },
      "size": 0,

      "dateCreated": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "data": {

      }
    }
  }
}
```

## List a Project's Data Filters

<a id="opIdlistProjectFilters"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/projects/string/string/filters/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/filters/`

Retrieve a list of filters for a given project.
`active` will be either a boolean or a list for the legacy browser filters.

<h3 id="list-a-projects-data-filters-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "id": "browser-extensions",
    "active": false
  },
  {
    "id": "filtered-transaction",
    "active": true
  },
  {
    "id": "legacy-browsers",
    "active": [
      "opera",
      "edge",
      "safari",
      "chrome",
      "ie",
      "opera_mini",
      "firefox",
      "android"
    ]
  },
  {
    "id": "localhost",
    "active": false
  },
  {
    "id": "web-crawlers",
    "active": true
  }
]
```

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

## Update an Inbound Data Filter

<a id="opIdupdateProjectFilter"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/projects/string/string/filters/string/' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "active": true,
    "subfilters": [
      "ie"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /api/0/projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/filters/{filter_id}/`

Update various inbound data filters for a project.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "active": true,
  "subfilters": [
    "ie"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-inbound-data-filter-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|filter_id|path|string|true|The type of filter toggle to update. The options are:<br>- `browser-extensions` - Filter out errors known to be caused by browser extensions.<br>- `localhost` - Filter out events coming from localhost. This applies to both IPv4 (``127.0.0.1``)<br>and IPv6 (``::1``) addresses.<br>- `filtered-transaction` - Filter out transactions for healthcheck and ping endpoints.<br>- `web-crawlers` - Filter out known web crawlers. Some crawlers may execute pages in incompatible<br>ways which cause errors that are unlikely to be seen by a normal user.<br>- `legacy-browser` - Filter out known errors from legacy browsers. Older browsers often give less<br>accurate information, and while they may report valid issues, the context to understand them is<br>incorrect or missing.<br>|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» active|body|boolean|false|Toggle the browser-extensions, localhost, filtered-transaction, or web-crawlers filter on or off.|
|» subfilters|body|[string]|false|<br>Specifies which legacy browser filters should be active. Anything excluded from the list will be<br>disabled. The options are:<br>- `ie` - Internet Explorer Version 11 and lower<br>- `edge` - Edge Version 110 and lower<br>- `safari` - Safari Version 15 and lower<br>- `firefox` - Firefox Version 110 and lower<br>- `chrome` - Chrome Version 110 and lower<br>- `opera` - Opera Version 99 and lower<br>- `android` - Android Version 3 and lower<br>- `opera_mini` - Opera Mini Version 34 and lower<br><br>Deprecated options:<br>- `ie_pre_9` - Internet Explorer Version 8 and lower<br>- `ie9` - Internet Explorer Version 9<br>- `ie10` - Internet Explorer Version 10<br>- `ie11` - Internet Explorer Version 11<br>- `safari_pre_6` - Safari Version 5 and lower<br>- `opera_pre_15` - Opera Version 14 and lower<br>- `opera_mini_pre_8` - Opera Mini Version 8 and lower<br>- `android_pre_4` - Android Version 3 and lower<br>- `edge_pre_79` - Edge Version 18 and lower (non Chromium based)<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» subfilters|ie|
|» subfilters|edge|
|» subfilters|safari|
|» subfilters|firefox|
|» subfilters|chrome|
|» subfilters|opera|
|» subfilters|android|
|» subfilters|opera_mini|
|» subfilters|ie_pre_9|
|» subfilters|ie9|
|» subfilters|ie10|
|» subfilters|ie11|
|» subfilters|opera_pre_15|
|» subfilters|android_pre_4|
|» subfilters|safari_pre_6|
|» subfilters|opera_mini_pre_8|
|» subfilters|edge_pre_79|

## Create a New Client Key

<a id="opIdcreateProjectKey"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/projects/string/string/keys/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "rateLimit": {
      "count": 0,
      "window": 0
    },
    "useCase": "user"
  }'
```

`POST /api/0/projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/keys/`

Create a new client key bound to a project.  The key's secret and public key
are generated by the server.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "rateLimit": {
    "count": 0,
    "window": 0
  },
  "useCase": "user"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-client-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string \| null|false|The optional name of the key. If not provided it will be automatically generated.|
|» rateLimit|body|object|false|Applies a rate limit to cap the number of errors accepted during a given time window. To<br>disable entirely set `rateLimit` to null.<br>```json<br>{<br>    "rateLimit": {<br>        "window": 7200, // time in seconds<br>        "count": 1000 // error cap<br>    }<br>}<br>```|
|» » count|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» » window|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» useCase|body|string|false|* `user`<br>* `profiling`<br>* `tempest`<br>* `demo`|

#### Enumerated Values

|---|---|
|» useCase|user|
|» useCase|profiling|
|» useCase|tempest|
|» useCase|demo|

## Update a Client Key

<a id="opIdupdateProjectKey"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/projects/string/string/keys/string/' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "isActive": true,
    "rateLimit": {
      "count": 0,
      "window": 0
    },
    "browserSdkVersion": "latest",
    "dynamicSdkLoaderOptions": {
      "hasReplay": true,
      "hasPerformance": true,
      "hasDebug": true,
      "hasFeedback": true,
      "hasLogsAndMetrics": true
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /api/0/projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/keys/{key_id}/`

Update various settings for a client key.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "isActive": true,
  "rateLimit": {
    "count": 0,
    "window": 0
  },
  "browserSdkVersion": "latest",
  "dynamicSdkLoaderOptions": {
    "hasReplay": true,
    "hasPerformance": true,
    "hasDebug": true,
    "hasFeedback": true,
    "hasLogsAndMetrics": true
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-client-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|key_id|path|string|true|The ID of the key to update.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|The name for the client key|
|» isActive|body|boolean|false|Activate or deactivate the client key.|
|» rateLimit|body|object|false|Applies a rate limit to cap the number of errors accepted during a given time window. To<br>disable entirely set `rateLimit` to null.<br>```json<br>{<br>    "rateLimit": {<br>        "window": 7200, // time in seconds<br>        "count": 1000 // error cap<br>    }<br>}<br>```|
|» » count|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» » window|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» browserSdkVersion|body|string|false|The Sentry Javascript SDK version to use. The currently supported options are:<br><br>* `latest` - Most recent version<br>* `7.x` - Version 7 releases|
|» dynamicSdkLoaderOptions|body|object|false|Configures multiple options for the Javascript Loader Script.<br>- `Performance Monitoring`<br>- `Debug Bundles & Logging`<br>- `Session Replay` - Note that the loader will load the ES6 bundle instead of the ES5 bundle.<br>- `User Feedback` - Note that the loader will load the ES6 bundle instead of the ES5 bundle.<br>- `Logs and Metrics` - Note that the loader will load the ES6 bundle instead of the ES5 bundle. Requires SDK >= 10.0.0.<br>```json<br>{<br>    "dynamicSdkLoaderOptions": {<br>        "hasReplay": true,<br>        "hasPerformance": true,<br>        "hasDebug": true,<br>        "hasFeedback": true,<br>        "hasLogsAndMetrics": true<br>    }<br>}<br>```|
|» » hasReplay|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » hasPerformance|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » hasDebug|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » hasFeedback|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » hasLogsAndMetrics|body|boolean|false|none|

|Parameter|Value|

|» browserSdkVersion|7.x|

## Update Ownership Configuration for a Project

<a id="opIdupdateProjectOwnership"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/projects/string/string/ownership/' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "raw": "string",
    "fallthrough": true,
    "autoAssignment": "string",
    "codeownersAutoSync": true
  }'
```

`PUT /api/0/projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/ownership/`

Updates ownership configurations for a project. Note that only the
attributes submitted are modified.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "raw": "string",
  "fallthrough": true,
  "autoAssignment": "string",
  "codeownersAutoSync": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-ownership-configuration-for-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» raw|body|string|false|Raw input for ownership configuration. See the [Ownership Rules Documentation](/product/issues/ownership-rules/) to learn more.|
|» fallthrough|body|boolean|false|A boolean determining who to assign ownership to when an ownership rule has no match. If set to `True`, all project members are made owners. Otherwise, no owners are set.|
|» autoAssignment|body|string|false|Auto-assignment settings. The available options are:<br>- Auto Assign to Issue Owner<br>- Auto Assign to Suspect Commits<br>- Turn off Auto-Assignment|
|» codeownersAutoSync|body|boolean|false|Set to `True` to sync issue owners with CODEOWNERS updates in a release.|

        },

          {
            "type": "user",
            "id": "2621754",
            "name": "jane.smith@org.com"
          }
        ]
      },
      {
        "matcher": {
          "type": "url",
          "pattern": "https://example.com/checkout"
        },
        "owners": [
          {
            "type": "user",

## List Repositories Linked to a Project

<a id="opIdlistProjectRepositories"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/projects/string/string/repo/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/repo/`

List all repositories linked to a project.

Pass `?includeMappingCount=1` to include the number of code path mappings
per repository. Omitting it keeps the query cheaper for callers that
only need the list of connections.

<h3 id="list-repositories-linked-to-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|includeMappingCount|query|string|false|When set to `1`, each row includes a `mappingCount` field with the number of code path mappings for that repository. Omitted by default to keep the response lightweight.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "id": "string",
    "integrationId": "string",
    "externalId": "string",
    "projectId": "string",
    "repositoryId": "string",
    "repoName": "string",
    "source": "string",
    "providerKey": "string",
    "mappingCount": 0
  }
]
```

<h3 id="list-repositories-linked-to-a-project-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
