Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» id|string|true|none|none|
|» integrationId|string \| null|true|none|none|
|» externalId|string \| null|true|none|none|
|» projectId|string|true|none|none|
|» repositoryId|string|true|none|none|

|» providerKey|string \| null|true|none|none|
|» mappingCount|integer|false|none|none|

## Link a Repository to a Project

<a id="opIdlinkProjectRepository"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/projects/string/string/repo/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "repositoryId": 0
  }'
```

`POST /api/0/projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/repo/`

Link a repository to a project. The repository must already exist
in the organization (connected via a VCS integration). Idempotent:
returns 200 if the link already exists, 201 if created.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "repositoryId": 0
}
```

<h3 id="link-a-repository-to-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» repositoryId|body|integer|true|The ID of the repository to link.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "projectId": "string",
  "repositoryId": "string",
  "source": "string",
  "created": true
}
```

## Retrieve Event Counts for a Project

<a id="opIdlistProjectStats"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/projects/string/string/stats/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/stats/`

Return a set of points representing a normalized timestamp and the number of
events seen in the period.

Query ranges are limited to Sentry's configured time-series resolutions.
This endpoint may change in the future without notice.

<h3 id="retrieve-event-counts-for-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|stat|query|string|false|The name of the stat to query. Defaults to `received`.|
|since|query|number(double)|false|A UNIX timestamp (in seconds) that sets the start of the query range.|
|until|query|number(double)|false|A UNIX timestamp (in seconds) that sets the end of the query range.|
|resolution|query|string|false|An explicit time series resolution.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|stat|blacklisted|
|stat|generated|
|stat|received|
|stat|rejected|
|resolution|10s|
|resolution|1d|
|resolution|1h|

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|id|query|string|true|The ID of the source to update.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of the source.<br><br>* `http` - SymbolServer (HTTP)<br>* `gcs` - Google Cloud Storage<br>* `s3` - Amazon S3<br>* `azure` - Azure Blob Storage|
|» name|body|string|true|The human-readable name of the source.|
|» id|body|string|false|The internal ID of the source. Must be distinct from all other source IDs and cannot start with '`sentry:`'. If this is not provided, a new UUID will be generated.|
|» layout|body|object|false|Layout settings for the source. This is required for HTTP, GCS, and S3 sources.<br><br>**`type`** ***(string)*** - The layout of the folder structure. The options are:<br>- `native` - Platform-Specific (SymStore / GDB / LLVM)<br>- `symstore` - Microsoft SymStore<br>- `symstore_index2` - Microsoft SymStore (with index2.txt)<br>- `ssqp` - Microsoft SSQP<br>- `unified` - Unified Symbol Server Layout<br>- `debuginfod` - debuginfod<br>- `nxsymstore` - Nintendo NXSymStore<br><br>**`casing`** ***(string)*** - The layout of the folder structure. The options are:<br>- `default` - Default (mixed case)<br>- `uppercase` - Uppercase<br>- `lowercase` - Lowercase<br><br>```json<br>{<br>    "layout": {<br>        "type": "native"<br>        "casing": "default"<br>    }<br>}<br>```|
|» » type|body|string|true|The source's layout type.<br><br>* `native`<br>* `symstore`<br>* `symstore_index2`<br>* `ssqp`<br>* `unified`<br>* `debuginfod`<br>* `slashsymbols`<br>* `nxsymstore`|
|» » casing|body|string|true|The source's casing rules.<br><br>* `lowercase`<br>* `uppercase`<br>* `default`|
|» filters|body|object|false|Filter settings for the source. This is optional for all sources.<br><br>**`filetypes`** ***(list)*** - A list of file types that can be found on this source. If this is left empty, all file types will be enabled. The options are:<br>- `pe` - Windows executable files<br>- `pdb` - Windows debug files<br>- `portablepdb` - .NET portable debug files<br>- `mach_code` - MacOS executable files<br>- `mach_debug` - MacOS debug files<br>- `elf_code` - ELF executable files<br>- `elf_debug` - ELF debug files<br>- `wasm_code` - WASM executable files<br>- `wasm_debug` - WASM debug files<br>- `breakpad` - Breakpad symbol files<br>- `sourcebundle` - Source code bundles<br>- `uuidmap` - Apple UUID mapping files<br>- `bcsymbolmap` - Apple bitcode symbol maps<br>- `il2cpp` - Unity IL2CPP mapping files<br>- `proguard` - ProGuard mapping files<br><br>**`path_patterns`** ***(list)*** - A list of glob patterns to check against the debug and code file paths of debug files. Only files that match one of these patterns will be requested from the source. If this is left empty, no path-based filtering takes place.<br><br>**`requires_checksum`** ***(boolean)*** - Whether this source requires a debug checksum to be sent with each request. Defaults to `false`.<br><br>```json<br>{<br>    "filters": {<br>        "filetypes": ["pe", "pdb", "portablepdb"],<br>        "path_patterns": ["*ffmpeg*"]<br>    }<br>}<br>```|
|» » filetypes|body|[string]|false|The file types enabled for the source.|
|» » path_patterns|body|[string]|false|The debug and code file paths enabled for the source.|
|» » requires_checksum|body|boolean|false|Whether the source requires debug checksums.|
|» url|body|string|false|The source's URL. Optional for HTTP sources, invalid for all others.|
|» username|body|string|false|The user name for accessing the source. Optional for HTTP sources, invalid for all others.|
|» password|body|string|false|The password for accessing the source. Optional for HTTP sources, invalid for all others.|
|» bucket|body|string|false|The GCS or S3 bucket where the source resides. Required for GCS and S3 source, invalid for HTTP sources.|
|» region|body|string|false|The source's [S3 region](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/s3.html). Required for S3 sources, invalid for all others.<br><br>* `us-east-2` - US East (Ohio)<br>* `us-east-1` - US East (N. Virginia)<br>* `us-west-1` - US West (N. California)<br>* `us-west-2` - US West (Oregon)<br>* `ap-east-1` - Asia Pacific (Hong Kong)<br>* `ap-south-1` - Asia Pacific (Mumbai)<br>* `ap-northeast-2` - Asia Pacific (Seoul)<br>* `ap-southeast-1` - Asia Pacific (Singapore)<br>* `ap-southeast-2` - Asia Pacific (Sydney)<br>* `ap-northeast-1` - Asia Pacific (Tokyo)<br>* `ca-central-1` - Canada (Central)<br>* `cn-north-1` - China (Beijing)<br>* `cn-northwest-1` - China (Ningxia)<br>* `eu-central-1` - EU (Frankfurt)<br>* `eu-west-1` - EU (Ireland)<br>* `eu-west-2` - EU (London)<br>* `eu-west-3` - EU (Paris)<br>* `eu-north-1` - EU (Stockholm)<br>* `sa-east-1` - South America (São Paulo)<br>* `us-gov-east-1` - AWS GovCloud (US-East)<br>* `us-gov-west-1` - AWS GovCloud (US)|
|» access_key|body|string|false|The [AWS Access Key](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/security-creds.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys).Required for S3 sources, invalid for all others.|
|» secret_key|body|string|false|The [AWS Secret Access Key](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/security-creds.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys).Required for S3 sources, invalid for all others.|
|» prefix|body|string|false|The GCS, Azure or [S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/using-prefixes.html) prefix. Optional for GCS, Azure and S3 sources, invalid for HTTP.|
|» client_email|body|string|false|The GCS email address for authentication. Required for GCS sources, invalid for all others.|
|» private_key|body|string|false|The GCS private key. Required for GCS sources if not using impersonated tokens. Invalid for all others.|
|» account|body|string|false|The Azure storage account name. Required for Azure sources, invalid for all others.|
|» container|body|string|false|The Azure blob container name. Required for Azure sources, invalid for all others.|
|» tenant_id|body|string|false|The Microsoft Entra tenant ID. Required for Azure sources, invalid for all others.|
|» client_id|body|string|false|The Microsoft Entra application (client) ID. Required for Azure sources, invalid for all others.|
|» client_secret|body|string|false|The Microsoft Entra client secret. Required for Azure sources, invalid for all others.|

The options are:<br>- `native` - Platform-Specific (SymStore / GDB / LLVM)<br>- `symstore` - Microsoft SymStore<br>- `symstore_index2` - Microsoft SymStore (with index2.txt)<br>- `ssqp` - Microsoft SSQP<br>- `unified` - Unified Symbol Server Layout<br>- `debuginfod` - debuginfod<br>- `nxsymstore` - Nintendo NXSymStore<br><br>**`casing`** ***(string)*** - The layout of the folder structure. The options are:<br>- `default` - Default (mixed case)<br>- `uppercase` - Uppercase<br>- `lowercase` - Lowercase<br><br>```json<br>{<br>    "layout": {<br>        "type": "native"<br>        "casing": "default"<br>    }<br>}<br>```|
|» » type|body|string|true|The source's layout type.<br><br>* `native`<br>* `symstore`<br>* `symstore_index2`<br>* `ssqp`<br>* `unified`<br>* `debuginfod`<br>* `slashsymbols`<br>* `nxsymstore`|
|» » casing|body|string|true|The source's casing rules.<br><br>* `lowercase`<br>* `uppercase`<br>* `default`|
|» filters|body|object|false|Filter settings for the source. This is optional for all sources.<br><br>**`filetypes`** ***(list)*** - A list of file types that can be found on this source. If this is left empty, all file types will be enabled. The options are:<br>- `pe` - Windows executable files<br>- `pdb` - Windows debug files<br>- `portablepdb` - .NET portable debug files<br>- `mach_code` - MacOS executable files<br>- `mach_debug` - MacOS debug files<br>- `elf_code` - ELF executable files<br>- `elf_debug` - ELF debug files<br>- `wasm_code` - WASM executable files<br>- `wasm_debug` - WASM debug files<br>- `breakpad` - Breakpad symbol files<br>- `sourcebundle` - Source code bundles<br>- `uuidmap` - Apple UUID mapping files<br>- `bcsymbolmap` - Apple bitcode symbol maps<br>- `il2cpp` - Unity IL2CPP mapping files<br>- `proguard` - ProGuard mapping files<br><br>**`path_patterns`** ***(list)*** - A list of glob patterns to check against the debug and code file paths of debug files. Only files that match one of these patterns will be requested from the source. If this is left empty, no path-based filtering takes place.<br><br>**`requires_checksum`** ***(boolean)*** - Whether this source requires a debug checksum to be sent with each request. Defaults to `false`.<br><br>```json<br>{<br>    "filters": {<br>        "filetypes": ["pe", "pdb", "portablepdb"],<br>        "path_patterns": ["*ffmpeg*"]<br>    }<br>}<br>```|
|» » filetypes|body|[string]|false|The file types enabled for the source.|

Required for S3 sources, invalid for all others.<br><br>* `us-east-2` - US East (Ohio)<br>* `us-east-1` - US East (N. Virginia)<br>* `us-west-1` - US West (N. ## Delete a Symbol Source from a Project

<a id="opIddeleteProjectSymbolSource"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/projects/string/string/symbol-sources/?id=string' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /api/0/projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/symbol-sources/`

Delete a custom symbol source from a project.

<h3 id="delete-a-symbol-source-from-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|id|query|string|true|The ID of the source to delete.|

<h3 id="delete-a-symbol-source-from-a-project-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|No Content|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

## Delete a Team from a Project

<a id="opIddeleteProjectTeam"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/projects/string/string/teams/string/' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /api/0/projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/teams/{team_id_or_slug}/`

Revoke a team's access to a project.

Note that Team Admins can only revoke access to teams they are admins of.

<h3 id="delete-a-team-from-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

## Create a New Project

<a id="opIdcreateTeamProject"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/teams/string/string/projects/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \

    "default_rules": true
  }'
```

`POST /api/0/teams/{organization_id_or_slug}/{team_id_or_slug}/projects/`

Create a new project bound to a team.

        Note: If your organization has disabled member project creation, the `org:write` scope or the Team Admin role on the team is required.
        

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "slug": "string",
  "platform": "string",
  "default_rules": true
}
```

|team_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the team the resource belongs to.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name for the project.|
|» slug|body|string \| null|false|Uniquely identifies a project and is used for the interface.<br>        If not provided, it is automatically generated from the name.|
|» platform|body|string \| null|false|The platform for the project.|
|» default_rules|body|boolean|false|<br>Defaults to true where the behavior is to alert the user on every new<br>issue. Setting this to false will turn this off and the user must create<br>their own alerts to be notified of new issues.<br>        |

## Submit User Feedback

<a id="opIdSubmit User Feedback"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/projects/string/string/user-feedback/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "event_id": "14bad9a2e3774046977a21440ddb39b2",
    "name": "Jane Schmidt",
    "email": "jane@empowerplant.io",
    "comments": "It broke!"
  }'
```

`POST /api/0/projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/user-feedback/`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

*This endpoint is DEPRECATED. We document it here for older SDKs and users who are still migrating to the [User Feedback Widget](https://docs.sentry.io/product/user-feedback/#user-feedback-widget) or [API](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/user-feedback/#user-feedback-api)(multi-platform). If you are a new user, do not use this endpoint - unless you don't have a JS frontend, and your platform's SDK does not offer a feedback API.*

Feedback must be received by the server no more than 30 minutes after the event was saved.

Additionally, within 5 minutes of submitting feedback it may also be overwritten. This is useful in situations where you may need to retry sending a request due to network failures.

If feedback is rejected due to a mutability threshold, a 409 status code will be returned.

Note: Feedback may be submitted with DSN authentication (see auth documentation).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "event_id": "14bad9a2e3774046977a21440ddb39b2",
  "name": "Jane Schmidt",
  "email": "jane@empowerplant.io",
  "comments": "It broke!"
}
```

<h3 id="submit-user-feedback-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» event_id|body|string|true|The event ID. This can be retrieved from the [beforeSend callback](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/configuration/filtering/#using-beforesend).|
|» name|body|string|true|User's name.|
|» email|body|string|true|User's email address.|
|» comments|body|string|true|Comments supplied by user.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "comments": "It broke!",
  "dateCreated": "2018-11-06T21:20:11.468Z",
  "email": "jane@example.com",
  "event": {
    "eventID": "14bad9a2e3774046977a21440ddb39b2",
    "id": null
  },
  "eventID": "14bad9a2e3774046977a21440ddb39b2",
  "id": "1",
  "issue": null,
  "name": "Jane Smith",
  "user": null
}
```

## Register a New Service Hook

<a id="opIdRegister a New Service Hook"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/projects/string/string/hooks/' \
```

`POST /api/0/projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/hooks/`

Register a new service hook on a project.

Events include:

- event.alert: An alert is generated for an event (via rules).
- event.created: A new event has been processed.

This endpoint requires the 'servicehooks' feature to be enabled for your project.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "url": "https://empowerplant.io/sentry-hook",
  "events": [
    "event.alert",
    "event.created"
  ]
}
```

|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the client keys belong to.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» url|body|string|true|The URL for the webhook.|
|» events|body|[string]|true|The events to subscribe to.|

`````````````````````````````````````````
## List an Organization's Issues

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationIssues"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/issues/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/issues/`

Return a list of issues for an organization. All parameters are supplied as query string parameters. A default query of `is:unresolved` is applied. To return all results, use an empty query value (i.e. ``?query=`). 

<h3 id="list-an-organizations-issues-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|
|project|query|[integer \| string]|false|The IDs or slugs of projects to filter by. Project slugs are unique within each organization. Omit this parameter to include all accessible projects. `-1` is also accepted to include all accessible projects.<br>For example, the following are valid parameters:<br>- `/?project=1234&project=56789`<br>- `/?project=android&project=javascript-react`<br>- `/?project=-1`<br>|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time for the query, will override the start & end parameters, a number followed by one of:<br>- `d` for days<br>- `h` for hours<br>- `m` for minutes<br>- `s` for seconds<br>- `w` for weeks<br><br>For example, `24h`, to mean query data starting from 24 hours ago to now.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|groupStatsPeriod|query|string|false|The timeline on which stats for the groups should be presented.|
|shortIdLookup|query|string|false|If this is set to `1` then the query will be parsed for issue short IDs. These may ignore other filters (e.g. projects), which is why it is an opt-in.|
|query|query|string|false|An optional search query for filtering issues. A default query will apply if no view/query is set. For all results use this parameter with an empty string.|
|viewId|query|string|false|The ID of the view to use. If no query is present, the view's query and filters will be applied.|
|sort|query|string|false|The sort order of the view. Options include 'Last Seen' (`date`), 'First Seen' (`new`), 'Trends' (`trends`), 'Events' (`freq`), 'Users' (`user`), 'Date Added' (`inbox`), and 'Recommended' (`recommended`).|
|limit|query|integer|false|The maximum number of issues to affect. The maximum is 100.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Additional data to include in the response.|
|collapse|query|[string]|false|Fields to remove from the response to improve query performance.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|

## Bulk Mutate an Organization's Issues

<a id="opIdupdateOrganizationIssues"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/issues/' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "inbox": true,
    "status": "resolved",
    "statusDetails": {
      "inNextRelease": true,
      "inRelease": "string",
      "inCommit": {
        "commit": "string",
        "repository": "string"
      },
      "ignoreDuration": 0,
      "ignoreCount": 0,
      "ignoreWindow": 0,
      "ignoreUserCount": 0,
      "ignoreUserWindow": 0
    },
    "substatus": "archived_until_escalating",
    "hasSeen": true,
    "isBookmarked": true,
    "isPublic": true,
    "isSubscribed": true,
    "merge": true,
    "discard": true,
    "assignedTo": "string",
    "priority": "low",
    "ignoreDuration": 0,
    "ignoreCount": 0,
    "ignoreWindow": 0,
    "ignoreUserCount": 0,
    "ignoreUserWindow": 0,
    "snoozeDuration": 0
  }'
```

`PUT /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/issues/`

Bulk mutate various attributes on a maxmimum of 1000 issues. 
- For non-status updates, the `id` query parameter is required. 
- For status updates, the `id` query parameter may be omitted to update issues that match the filtering. 
If any IDs are out of scope, the data won't be mutated but the endpoint will still produce a successful response. For example, if no issues were found matching the criteria, a HTTP 204 is returned.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "inbox": true,
  "status": "resolved",
  "statusDetails": {
    "inNextRelease": true,
    "inRelease": "string",
    "inCommit": {
      "commit": "string",
      "repository": "string"
    },
    "ignoreDuration": 0,
    "ignoreCount": 0,
    "ignoreWindow": 0,
    "ignoreUserCount": 0,
    "ignoreUserWindow": 0
  },

  "snoozeDuration": 0
}

<h3 id="bulk-mutate-an-organizations-issues-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|
|project|query|[integer \| string]|false|The IDs or slugs of projects to filter by. Project slugs are unique within each organization. |» » » commit|body|string|true|The SHA of the resolving commit.|
|» » » repository|body|string|true|The name of the repository (as it appears in Sentry).|
|» » ignoreDuration|body|integer|true|Ignore the issue until for this many minutes.|
|» » ignoreCount|body|integer|true|Ignore the issue until it has occurred this many times in `ignoreWindow` minutes.|

|» » ignoreUserWindow|body|integer|true|Ignore the issue until it has affected `ignoreUserCount` users in this many minutes. (Max: 1 week)|
|» substatus|body|string \| null|true|The new substatus of the issue.<br><br>* `archived_until_escalating`<br>* `archived_until_condition_met`<br>* `archived_forever`<br>* `escalating`<br>* `ongoing`<br>* `regressed`<br>* `new`|
|» hasSeen|body|boolean|true|If true, marks the issue as seen by the requestor.|
|» isBookmarked|body|boolean|true|If true, bookmarks the issue for the requestor.|
|» isPublic|body|boolean|true|If true, publishes the issue.|
|» isSubscribed|body|boolean|true|If true, subscribes the requestor to the issue.|
|» merge|body|boolean|true|If true, merges the issues together.|
|» discard|body|boolean|true|If true, discards the issues instead of updating them.|

## Bulk Remove an Organization's Issues

<a id="opIddeleteOrganizationIssues"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/issues/' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/issues/`

Permanently remove the given issues. If IDs are provided, queries and filtering will be ignored. If any IDs are out of scope, the data won't be mutated but the endpoint will still produce a successful response. For example, if no issues were found matching the criteria, a HTTP 204 is returned.

<h3 id="bulk-remove-an-organizations-issues-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|
|project|query|[integer \| string]|false|The IDs or slugs of projects to filter by. Project slugs are unique within each organization. Omit this parameter to include all accessible projects. `-1` is also accepted to include all accessible projects.<br>For example, the following are valid parameters:<br>- `/?project=1234&project=56789`<br>- `/?project=android&project=javascript-react`<br>- `/?project=-1`<br>|
|id|query|[integer]|false|The list of issue IDs to be removed. If not provided, it will attempt to remove the first 1000 issues.|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time for the query, will override the start & end parameters, a number followed by one of:<br>- `d` for days<br>- `h` for hours<br>- `m` for minutes<br>- `s` for seconds<br>- `w` for weeks<br><br>For example, `24h`, to mean query data starting from 24 hours ago to now.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|query|query|string|false|An optional search query for filtering issues. A default query will apply if no view/query is set. For all results use this parameter with an empty string.|
|viewId|query|string|false|The ID of the view to use. If no query is present, the view's query and filters will be applied.|
|sort|query|string|false|The sort order of the view. Options include 'Last Seen' (`date`), 'First Seen' (`new`), 'Trends' (`trends`), 'Events' (`freq`), 'Users' (`user`), 'Date Added' (`inbox`), and 'Recommended' (`recommended`).|
|limit|query|integer|false|The maximum number of issues to affect. The maximum is 100.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|date|
|sort|freq|
|sort|inbox|
|sort|new|
|sort|recommended|
|sort|trends|
|sort|user|

## List a Project's Error Events

```bash

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/events/`

Return a list of events bound to a project.

<h3 id="list-a-projects-error-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time for the query, will override the start & end parameters, a number followed by one of:<br>- `d` for days<br>- `h` for hours<br>- `m` for minutes<br>- `s` for seconds<br>- `w` for weeks<br><br>For example, `24h`, to mean query data starting from 24 hours ago to now.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|
|full|query|boolean|false|Specify true to include the full event body, including the stacktrace, in the event payload. When true, the page size is capped at 10.|
|sample|query|boolean|false|Return events in pseudo-random order. This is deterministic so an identical query will always return the same events in the same order.|

`GET /api/0/projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/events/{event_id}/`

## List an Event's Attachments

<a id="opIdlistProjectEventAttachments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/projects/string/string/events/string/attachments/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/events/{event_id}/attachments/`

Retrieve a list of attachments uploaded for a given event.

Requires the `event-attachments` organization feature.

<h3 id="list-an-events-attachments-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|event_id|path|string|true|The ID of the event. It is a 32-character hexadecimal string as reported by the client.|
|query|query|string|false|Filter the attachments by name (substring match) or by attachment kind. Use `is:screenshot` to restrict the results to screenshot attachments.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "id": "1234",

## Retrieve an Event Attachment

<a id="opIdgetProjectEventAttachment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/projects/string/string/events/string/attachments/string/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/events/{event_id}/attachments/{attachment_id}/`

Retrieve metadata for a single attachment on an event, or download its
contents by passing the `download` query parameter.

Requires the `event-attachments` organization feature.

<h3 id="retrieve-an-event-attachment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|event_id|path|string|true|The ID of the event. It is a 32-character hexadecimal string as reported by the client.|
|attachment_id|path|string|true|The numeric ID of the attachment, as returned from the attachments list endpoint.|
|download|query|string|false|If this parameter is present, the response will be a binary file download instead of JSON metadata. The value does not matter — any value (including empty) triggers the download. Depending on where the attachment is stored, the response may be a redirect to the storage service, so clients must follow redirects.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "1234",
  "event_id": "9b29bbe17e9d4ee3a6d0fe9b2e8a3b1c",
  "type": "event.attachment",
  "name": "screenshot.png",
  "mimetype": "image/png",
  "dateCreated": "2026-04-15T18:22:31Z",
  "size": 248137,
  "headers": {
    "Content-Type": "image/png"
  },
  "sha1": "d3f299af02d6abbe92dd8368bab781824a9702ed"
}
```

## List a Project's Issues

<a id="opIdList a Project's Issues"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/projects/string/string/issues/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/issues/`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**Deprecated**: This endpoint has been replaced with the [Organization Issues endpoint](/api/events/list-an-organizations-issues/) which
supports filtering on project and additional functionality.

Return a list of issues (groups) bound to a project.  All parameters are supplied as query string parameters. 

 A default query of ``is:unresolved`` is applied. To return results with other statuses send an new query value (i.e. ``?query=`` for all results).

The ``statsPeriod`` parameter can be used to select the timeline stats which should be present. Possible values are: ``""`` (disable),``"24h"`` (default), ``"14d"``

User feedback items from the [User Feedback Widget](https://docs.sentry.io/product/user-feedback/#user-feedback-widget) are built off the issue platform, so to return a list of user feedback items for a specific project, filter for `issue.category:feedback`.

<h3 id="list-a-projects-issues-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the issues belong to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the issues belong to.|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|An optional stat period (can be one of `"24h"`, `"14d"`, and `""`), defaults to "24h" if not provided.|
|shortIdLookup|query|boolean|false|If this is set to true then short IDs are looked up by this function as well. This can cause the return value of the function to return an event issue of a different project which is why this is an opt-in. Set to 1 to enable.|
|query|query|string|false|An optional Sentry structured search query. If not provided an implied `"is:unresolved"` is assumed.|
|hashes|query|string|false|A list of hashes of groups to return. Is not compatible with 'query' parameter. The maximum number of hashes that can be sent is 100. If more are sent, only the first 100 will be used.|
|sort|query|string|false|The sort order of the issues. Options include 'Last Seen' (`date`), 'First Seen' (`new`), 'Trends' (`trends`), 'Events' (`freq`), 'Users' (`user`), and 'Recommended' (`recommended`).|
|limit|query|integer|false|The maximum number of issues to return. The maximum is 100.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|date|
|sort|new|
|sort|trends|
|sort|freq|
|sort|user|
|sort|recommended|

## Bulk Mutate a List of Issues

<a id="opIdBulk Mutate a List of Issues"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/projects/string/string/issues/' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "isPublic": false,
    "status": "unresolved"
  }'
```

`PUT /api/0/projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/issues/`

Bulk mutate various attributes on issues.  The list of issues to modify is given through the `id` query parameter.  It is repeated for each issue that should be modified.

- For non-status updates, the `id` query parameter is required.
- For status updates, the `id` query parameter may be omitted
for a batch "update all" query.
- An optional `status` query parameter may be used to restrict
mutations to only events with the given status.

The following attributes can be modified and are supplied as JSON object in the body:

If any IDs are out of scope this operation will succeed without any data mutation.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "isPublic": false,
  "status": "unresolved"
}
```

<h3 id="bulk-mutate-a-list-of-issues-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the issues belong to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the issues belong to.|
|id|query|integer|false|A list of IDs of the issues to be mutated. This parameter shall be repeated for each issue. It is optional only if a status is mutated in which case an implicit update all is assumed.|
|status|query|string|false|Optionally limits the query to issues of the specified status. Valid values are `"resolved"`, `"reprocessing"`, `"unresolved"`, and `"ignored"`.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» status|body|string|false|The new status for the issues. Valid values are `"resolved"`, `"resolvedInNextRelease"`, `"unresolved"`, and `"ignored"`.|
|» statusDetails|body|object|false|Additional details about the resolution. Valid values are `"inRelease"`, `"inNextRelease"`, `"inCommit"`, `"ignoreDuration"`, `"ignoreCount"`, `"ignoreWindow"`, `"ignoreUserCount"`, and `"ignoreUserWindow"`.|
|» » inRelease|body|string|false|none|
|» » inNextRelease|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » inCommit|body|string|false|none|
|» » ignoreDuration|body|integer|false|none|
|» » ignoreCount|body|integer|false|none|
|» » ignoreWindow|body|integer|false|none|
|» » ignoreUserCount|body|integer|false|none|
|» » ignoreUserWindow|body|integer|false|none|
|» ignoreDuration|body|integer|false|The number of minutes to ignore this issue.|
|» isPublic|body|boolean|false|Sets the issue to public or private.|
|» merge|body|boolean|false|Allows to merge or unmerge different issues.|
|» assignedTo|body|string|false|The actor ID (or username) of the user or team that should be assigned to this issue.|
|» hasSeen|body|boolean|false|In case this API call is invoked with a user context this allows changing of the flag that indicates if the user has seen the event.|
|» isBookmarked|body|boolean|false|In case this API call is invoked with a user context this allows changing of the bookmark flag.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "isPublic": false,
  "status": "unresolved",
  "statusDetails": {}
}
```

<h3 id="bulk-mutate-a-list-of-issues-responses">Responses</h3>

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /api/0/projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/issues/`

Permanently remove the given issues. The list of issues to modify is given through the `id` query parameter.  It is repeated for each issue that should be removed.

Only queries by 'id' are accepted.

If any IDs are out of scope this operation will succeed without any data mutation.

<h3 id="bulk-remove-a-list-of-issues-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the issues belong to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the issues belong to.|
|id|query|integer|false|A list of IDs of the issues to be removed. This parameter shall be repeated for each issue, e.g. `?id=1&id=2&id=3`. If this parameter is not provided, it will attempt to remove the first 1000 issues.|

<h3 id="bulk-remove-a-list-of-issues-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Success|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Project not found|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
auth_token
</aside>

## List a Tag's Values for an Issue

## Update an Issue

<a id="opIdupdateOrganizationIssue"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/issues/string/' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "inbox": true,
    "status": "resolved",
    "statusDetails": {
      "inNextRelease": true,
      "inRelease": "string",
      "inCommit": {
        "commit": "string",
        "repository": "string"
      },
      "ignoreDuration": 0,
      "ignoreCount": 0,
      "ignoreWindow": 0,
      "ignoreUserCount": 0,
      "ignoreUserWindow": 0
    },
    "substatus": "archived_until_escalating",
    "hasSeen": true,
    "isBookmarked": true,
    "isPublic": true,
    "isSubscribed": true,
    "merge": true,
    "discard": true,
    "assignedTo": "string",
    "priority": "low",
    "ignoreDuration": 0,
    "ignoreCount": 0,
    "ignoreWindow": 0,
    "ignoreUserCount": 0,
    "ignoreUserWindow": 0,
    "snoozeDuration": 0
  }'
```

`PUT /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/issues/{issue_id}/`

Update an individual issue's attributes. Only the attributes submitted
are modified.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "inbox": true,
  "status": "resolved",
  "statusDetails": {
    "inNextRelease": true,
    "inRelease": "string",
    "inCommit": {
      "commit": "string",
      "repository": "string"
    },
    "ignoreDuration": 0,
    "ignoreCount": 0,
    "ignoreWindow": 0,
    "ignoreUserCount": 0,
    "ignoreUserWindow": 0
  },
  "substatus": "archived_until_escalating",
  "hasSeen": true,
  "isBookmarked": true,
  "isPublic": true,
  "isSubscribed": true,
  "merge": true,
  "discard": true,
  "assignedTo": "string",
  "priority": "low",
  "ignoreDuration": 0,
  "ignoreCount": 0,
  "ignoreWindow": 0,
  "ignoreUserCount": 0,
  "ignoreUserWindow": 0,
  "snoozeDuration": 0
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-issue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|issue_id|path|string|true|The ID of the issue you'd like to query.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» inbox|body|boolean|true|If true, marks the issue as reviewed by the requestor.|
|» status|body|string|true|Limit mutations to only issues with the given status.<br><br>* `resolved`<br>* `unresolved`<br>* `ignored`<br>* `resolvedInNextRelease`<br>* `muted`|
|» statusDetails|body|object|true|Additional details about the resolution. Status detail updates that include release data are only allowed for issues within a single project.|
|» » inNextRelease|body|boolean|true|If true, marks the issue as resolved in the next release.|
|» » inRelease|body|string|true|The version of the release that the issue should be resolved in.If set to `latest`, the latest release will be used.|
|» » inCommit|body|object|false|The commit data that the issue should use for resolution.|
|» » » commit|body|string|true|The SHA of the resolving commit.|
|» » » repository|body|string|true|The name of the repository (as it appears in Sentry).|
|» » ignoreDuration|body|integer|true|Ignore the issue until for this many minutes.|
|» » ignoreCount|body|integer|true|Ignore the issue until it has occurred this many times in `ignoreWindow` minutes.|
|» » ignoreWindow|body|integer|true|Ignore the issue until it has occurred `ignoreCount` times in this many minutes. (Max: 1 week)|
|» » ignoreUserCount|body|integer|true|Ignore the issue until it has affected this many users in `ignoreUserWindow` minutes.|
|» » ignoreUserWindow|body|integer|true|Ignore the issue until it has affected `ignoreUserCount` users in this many minutes. (Max: 1 week)|
|» substatus|body|string \| null|true|The new substatus of the issue.<br><br>* `archived_until_escalating`<br>* `archived_until_condition_met`<br>* `archived_forever`<br>* `escalating`<br>* `ongoing`<br>* `regressed`<br>* `new`|
|» hasSeen|body|boolean|true|If true, marks the issue as seen by the requestor.|
|» isBookmarked|body|boolean|true|If true, bookmarks the issue for the requestor.|
|» isPublic|body|boolean|true|If true, publishes the issue.|
|» isSubscribed|body|boolean|true|If true, subscribes the requestor to the issue.|
|» merge|body|boolean|true|If true, merges the issues together.|
|» discard|body|boolean|true|If true, discards the issues instead of updating them.|
|» assignedTo|body|string|true|The user or team that should be assigned to the issues. Values take the form of `<user_id>`, `user:<user_id>`, `<username>`, `<user_primary_email>`, or `team:<team_id>`.|
|» priority|body|string|true|The priority that should be set for the issues<br><br>* `low`<br>* `medium`<br>* `high`|
|» ignoreDuration|body|integer|true|Ignore the issue for this many minutes.|
|» ignoreCount|body|integer|true|Ignore the issue until it is seen this many more times.|
|» ignoreWindow|body|integer|true|Window in minutes over which `ignoreCount` is measured. Maximum is 7 days.|
|» ignoreUserCount|body|integer|true|Ignore the issue until it affects this many more users.|
|» ignoreUserWindow|body|integer|true|Window in minutes over which `ignoreUserCount` is measured. Maximum is 7 days.|
|» snoozeDuration|body|integer \| null|true|Snooze the issue for this many minutes.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» status|resolved|
|» status|unresolved|
|» status|ignored|
|» status|resolvedInNextRelease|
|» status|muted|
|» substatus|archived_until_escalating|
|» substatus|archived_until_condition_met|
|» substatus|archived_forever|
|» substatus|escalating|
|» substatus|ongoing|
|» substatus|regressed|
|» substatus|new|
|» substatus|null|

|» priority|medium|
|» priority|high|

## Remove an Issue

<a id="opIddeleteOrganizationIssue"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/issues/string/' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/issues/{issue_id}/`

Asynchronously queue an individual issue for deletion.

<h3 id="remove-an-issue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|issue_id|path|string|true|The ID of the issue you'd like to query.|

<h3 id="remove-an-issue-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Accepted|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

</aside>

## List an Issue's Events

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationIssueEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/issues/string/events/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/issues/{issue_id}/events/`

Return a list of error events bound to an issue

<h3 id="list-an-issues-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|issue_id|path|string|true|The ID of the issue you'd like to query.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time for the query, will override the start & end parameters, a number followed by one of:<br>- `d` for days<br>- `h` for hours<br>- `m` for minutes<br>- `s` for seconds<br>- `w` for weeks<br><br>For example, `24h`, to mean query data starting from 24 hours ago to now.|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|
|full|query|boolean|false|Specify true to include the full event body, including the stacktrace, in the event payload. When true, the page size is capped at 10.|
|sample|query|boolean|false|Return events in pseudo-random order. This is deterministic so an identical query will always return the same events in the same order.|
|query|query|string|false|An optional search query for filtering events. See [search syntax](https://docs.sentry.io/concepts/search/) and queryable event properties at [Sentry Search Documentation](https://docs.sentry.io/concepts/search/searchable-properties/events/) for more information. An example query might be `query=transaction:foo AND release:abc`|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Limit the number of rows to return in the result. Default and maximum allowed is 100.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|

## Retrieve an Issue Event

<a id="opIdgetOrganizationIssueEvent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/issues/string/events/latest/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/issues/{issue_id}/events/{event_id}/`

Retrieves the details of an issue event.

<h3 id="retrieve-an-issue-event-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|issue_id|path|string|true|The ID of the issue you'd like to query.|
|event_id|path|string|true|The ID of the event to retrieve, or 'latest', 'oldest', or 'recommended'.|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|
|collapse|query|[string]|false|Parts of the response to skip computing. Specify `adjacentEvents` to skip looking up the neighboring events in the issue; `nextEventID` and `previousEventID` are then always `null`. Unknown values are ignored.|
|llmFormat|query|string|false|If set, adds a `formatted` field to the response with the event rendered as the requested format for LLM consumption.|

|event_id|latest|
|event_id|oldest|
|event_id|recommended|
|collapse|adjacentEvents|
|llmFormat|json|
|llmFormat|markdown|
|llmFormat|xml|

## List an Issue's Hashes

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationIssueHashes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/issues/string/hashes/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/issues/{issue_id}/hashes/`

List the hashes that make up an issue. Each hash represents a grouping
signature used to aggregate individual events into this issue.

<h3 id="list-an-issues-hashes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|issue_id|path|string|true|The ID of the issue you'd like to query.|
|full|query|boolean|false|Specify true to include the full event body, including the stacktrace, in the event payload. When true, the page size is capped at 10.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json

## Retrieve Tag Details

<a id="opIdgetOrganizationIssueTag"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/issues/string/tags/string/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/issues/{issue_id}/tags/{key}/`

Return a list of values associated with this key for an issue. When paginated can return at most 1000 values.

<h3 id="retrieve-tag-details-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issue_id|path|string|true|The ID of the issue you'd like to query.|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|key|path|string|true|The tag key to look the values up for.|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "key": "flavors",
  "name": "Flavors",
  "uniqueValues": 2,
  "totalValues": 3,
  "topValues": [
    {
      "key": "strawberry",
      "name": "Strawberry",
      "value": "strawberry",
      "count": 2,
      "lastSeen": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "firstSeen": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    },
    {
      "key": "vanilla",
      "name": "Vanilla",
      "value": "vanilla",
      "count": 1,
      "lastSeen": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "firstSeen": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

## Assemble an Artifact Bundle

<a id="opIdassembleOrganizationArtifactBundle"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/artifactbundle/assemble/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "projects": [
      "string"
    ],
    "checksum": "string",
    "chunks": [
      "string"
    ],
    "version": "string",
    "dist": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/artifactbundle/assemble/`

**Experimental:** This API is under active development and may change.

Assemble previously uploaded chunks into an artifact bundle, such as source maps, and
store its debug IDs.

The response reports the bundle's `state`. If chunks are missing, upload them and send
the request again. Repeat the request to poll until the state is `ok` or `error`.
Resending an identical request is safe: a bundle that is already assembling or
assembled reports its state instead of starting a new job.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "projects": [
    "string"
  ],
  "checksum": "string",
  "chunks": [
    "string"
  ],
  "version": "string",
  "dist": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="assemble-an-artifact-bundle-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» projects|body|[string]|true|The IDs or slugs of the projects the bundle belongs to.|
|» checksum|body|string|true|The SHA-1 checksum of the whole bundle.|
|» chunks|body|[string]|true|The SHA-1 checksums of the bundle's chunks, in order. Upload missing chunks with the chunk upload endpoint. Send an empty list to poll the bundle's state.|
|» version|body|string|false|The release to associate the bundle with.|
|» dist|body|string|false|The distribution to associate the bundle with. Requires `version`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "state": "string",
  "missingChunks": [
    "string"
  ],
  "detail": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="assemble-an-artifact-bundle-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<h3 id="assemble-an-artifact-bundle-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|state|string|true|none|none|
|missingChunks|[string]|true|none|none|
|detail|string \| null|false|none|none|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
auth_token
</aside>

## Retrieve Statuses of Release Thresholds (Alpha)

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationReleaseThresholdStatuses"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/release-threshold-statuses/?start=1970-01-01T00%3A00%3A00Z&end=1970-01-01T00%3A00%3A00Z' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/release-threshold-statuses/`

**Experimental:** This API is under active development and may change.

List all derived statuses of releases that fall within the provided start/end datetimes.

Constructs a response key'd off \{`release_version`\}-\{`project_slug`\} that lists thresholds with their status for *specified* projects.
Each returned enriched threshold will contain the full serialized `release_threshold` instance as well as it's derived health statuses.

<h3 id="retrieve-statuses-of-release-thresholds-alpha-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|true|The start of the time series range as an explicit datetime, either in UTC ISO8601 or epoch seconds. Use along with `end`.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|true|The inclusive end of the time series range as an explicit datetime, either in UTC ISO8601 or epoch seconds. Use along with `start`.|
|environment|query|[string]|false|A list of environment names to filter your results by.|
|projectSlug|query|[string]|false|A list of project slugs to filter your results by.|
|release|query|[string]|false|A list of release versions to filter your results by.|
|project|query|[integer \| string]|false|A list of project IDs or slugs to filter your results by.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

## List an Organization's Releases

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationReleases"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/releases/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/releases/`

Return a list of releases for a given organization, sorted by most recent.

<h3 id="list-an-organizations-releases-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project|query|[integer \| string]|false|The IDs or slugs of projects to filter by. Project slugs are unique within each organization. Omit this parameter to include all accessible projects. `-1` is also accepted to include all accessible projects.<br>For example, the following are valid parameters:<br>- `/?project=1234&project=56789`<br>- `/?project=android&project=javascript-react`<br>- `/?project=-1`<br>|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|
|query|query|string|false|Case-insensitive substring match against the release version.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Limit the number of rows to return in the result. Default and maximum allowed is 100.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|

## Create a New Release for an Organization

<a id="opIdcreateOrganizationRelease"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/releases/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "version": "string",
    "projects": [
      "string"
    ],
    "ref": "string",
    "url": "http://example.com",
    "dateReleased": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "commits": [
      {
        "id": "string",
        "repository": "string",
        "message": "string",
        "author_name": "string",
        "author_email": "string",
        "timestamp": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "patch_set": [
          {
            "path": "string",
            "type": "s"
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "status": "string",
    "owner": "string",
    "headCommits": [
      {
        "currentId": "string",
        "repository": "string",
        "previousId": "string"
      }
    ],
    "refs": [
      {
        "commit": "string",
        "repository": "string",
        "previousCommit": "string"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/releases/`

Create a new release for the given organization. Releases are used by Sentry to
improve error reporting by correlating first-seen events with the release that may
have introduced them, and are required for source maps and other debug features.

Release versions that are the same across multiple projects within an organization
are treated as the same release in Sentry.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "version": "string",
  "projects": [
    "string"
  ],
  "ref": "string",
  "url": "http://example.com",
  "dateReleased": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "commits": [
    {
      "id": "string",
      "repository": "string",
      "message": "string",
      "author_name": "string",
      "author_email": "string",
      "timestamp": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "patch_set": [
        {
          "path": "string",
          "type": "s"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "status": "string",
  "owner": "string",
  "headCommits": [
    {
      "currentId": "string",
      "repository": "string",
      "previousId": "string"
    }
  ],
  "refs": [
    {
      "commit": "string",
      "repository": "string",
      "previousCommit": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-release-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» version|body|string|true|A version identifier for this release. Can be a version number, a commit hash, and so on.|
|» projects|body|[string]|true|A list of project slugs that are involved in this release.|
|» ref|body|string \| null|false|An optional commit reference. This is useful if a tagged version has been provided.|
|» url|body|string(uri) \| null|false|A URL that points to the release. For instance, this can be the path to an online interface to the source code, such as a GitHub URL.|
|» dateReleased|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|An optional date that indicates when the release went live.  If not provided the current time is used.|
|» commits|body|[object]|false|An optional list of commit data to be associated.|
|» » id|body|string|true|none|
|» » repository|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » message|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » author_name|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » author_email|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » timestamp|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|
|» » patch_set|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » » path|body|string|true|none|
|» » » type|body|string|true|none|
|» status|body|string|false|The status of the release. Can be `open` or `archived`.|
|» owner|body|string|false|The username of the user to set as the release owner.|
|» headCommits|body|[object]|false|(Deprecated) Use `refs` instead. An optional list of head commits to associate with the release, one per repository.|
|» » currentId|body|string|true|none|
|» » repository|body|string|true|none|
|» » previousId|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» refs|body|[object]|false|An optional list of commit references, one per repository, used to associate commits with the release.|
|» » commit|body|string|true|none|
|» » repository|body|string|true|none|
|» » previousCommit|body|string \| null|false|none|

## Retrieve an Organization's Release

<a id="opIdgetOrganizationRelease"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/releases/string/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/releases/{version}/`

Return details on an individual release.

<h3 id="retrieve-an-organizations-release-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|version|path|string|true|The version identifier of the release|
|project_id|query|string|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated. Use project instead.|
|project|query|integer \| string|false|The project ID or slug to filter by. Overrides project_id when both are sent.|
|health|query|boolean|false|Whether or not to include health data with the release. By default, this is false.|
|adoptionStages|query|boolean|false|Whether or not to include adoption stages with the release. By default, this is false.|
|summaryStatsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time used to query summary stats for the release. By default, this is 14d.|
|healthStatsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time used to query health stats for the release. By default, this is 24h if health is enabled.|
|sort|query|string|false|The field used to sort results by. By default, this is `date`.|
|status|query|string|false|Release statuses that you can filter by.|

## Update an Organization's Release

<a id="opIdupdateOrganizationRelease"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/releases/string/' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "ref": "string",
    "url": "http://example.com",
    "dateReleased": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "commits": [
      {
        "id": "string",
        "repository": "string",
        "message": "string",
        "author_name": "string",
        "author_email": "string",
        "timestamp": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "patch_set": [
          {
            "path": "string",
            "type": "s"
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "status": "string",
    "headCommits": [
      {
        "currentId": "string",
        "repository": "string",
        "previousId": "string"
      }
    ],
    "refs": [
      {
        "commit": "string",
        "repository": "string",
        "previousCommit": "string"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/releases/{version}/`

Update a release. This can change some metadata associated with
the release (the ref, url, and dates).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ref": "string",
  "url": "http://example.com",
  "dateReleased": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "commits": [
    {
      "id": "string",
      "repository": "string",
      "message": "string",
      "author_name": "string",
      "author_email": "string",
      "timestamp": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "patch_set": [
        {
          "path": "string",
          "type": "s"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "status": "string",
  "headCommits": [
    {
      "currentId": "string",
      "repository": "string",
      "previousId": "string"
    }
  ],
  "refs": [
    {
      "commit": "string",
      "repository": "string",
      "previousCommit": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-organizations-release-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|version|path|string|true|The version identifier of the release|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» ref|body|string \| null|false|An optional commit reference. This is useful if a tagged version has been provided.|
|» url|body|string(uri) \| null|false|A URL that points to the release. For instance, this can be the path to an online interface to the source code, such as a GitHub URL.|
|» dateReleased|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|An optional date that indicates when the release went live.  If not provided the current time is used.|
|» commits|body|[object]|false|An optional list of commit data to be associated.|
|» » id|body|string|true|none|
|» » repository|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » message|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » author_name|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » author_email|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » timestamp|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|
|» » patch_set|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » » path|body|string|true|none|
|» » » type|body|string|true|none|
|» status|body|string|false|The status of the release. Can be `open` or `archived`.|
|» headCommits|body|[object]|false|Deprecated, use `commits`. Head commits to associate with the release.|
|» » currentId|body|string|true|none|
|» » repository|body|string|true|none|
|» » previousId|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» refs|body|[object]|false|An optional way to indicate the start and end commits for each repository included in a release. Head commits must include parameters ``repository`` and ``commit`` (the HEAD SHA). For GitLab repositories, please use the Group name instead of the slug. They can optionally include ``previousCommit`` (the SHA of the HEAD of the previous release), which should be specified if this is the first time you've sent commit data.|
|» » commit|body|string|true|none|
|» » repository|body|string|true|none|
|» » previousCommit|body|string \| null|false|none|

## Delete an Organization's Release

<a id="opIddeleteOrganizationRelease"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/releases/string/' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/releases/{version}/`

Permanently remove a release and all of its files.

<h3 id="delete-an-organizations-release-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|version|path|string|true|The version identifier of the release|

<h3 id="delete-an-organizations-release-responses">Responses</h3>

|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/releases/{version}/deploys/`

## Create a Deploy

<a id="opIdcreateOrganizationReleaseDeploy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/releases/string/deploys/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "environment": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "url": "http://example.com",

## Retrieve Release Health Session Statistics

<a id="opIdgetOrganizationSessions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/sessions/?field=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/sessions/`

Returns a time series of release health session statistics for projects bound to an organization.

The interval and date range are subject to certain restrictions and rounding rules.

The date range is rounded to align with the interval, and is rounded to at least one
hour. The interval can at most be one day and at least one hour currently. It has to cleanly
divide one day, for rounding reasons.

Because of technical limitations, this endpoint returns
at most 10000 data points. For example, if you select a 90 day window grouped by releases,
you will see at most `floor(10k / (90 + 1)) = 109` releases. To get more results, reduce the
`statsPeriod`.

<h3 id="retrieve-release-health-session-statistics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|field|query|[string]|true|The list of fields to query.<br><br>The available fields are<br>- `sum(session)`<br>- `count_unique(user)`<br>- `avg`, `p50`, `p75`, `p90`, `p95`, `p99`, `max` applied to `session.duration`. For example, `p99(session.duration)`. Session duration is [no longer being recorded](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/discussions/42716) as of on Jan 12, 2023. Returned data may be incomplete.<br>- `crash_rate`, `crash_free_rate` applied to `user` or `session`. For example, `crash_free_rate(user)`<br>|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time for the query, will override the start & end parameters, a number followed by one of:<br>- `d` for days<br>- `h` for hours<br>- `m` for minutes<br>- `s` for seconds<br>- `w` for weeks<br><br>For example, `24h`, to mean query data starting from 24 hours ago to now.|
|project|query|[integer \| string]|false|The IDs or slugs of projects to filter by. Project slugs are unique within each organization. Omit this parameter to include all accessible projects. `-1` is also accepted to include all accessible projects.<br>For example, the following are valid parameters:<br>- `/?project=1234&project=56789`<br>- `/?project=android&project=javascript-react`<br>- `/?project=-1`<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of groups to return per request.|
|interval|query|string|false|Resolution of the time series, given in the same format as `statsPeriod`.<br><br>The default and<br>        the minimum interval is `1h`.|
|groupBy|query|[string]|false|The list of properties to group by.<br><br>The available groupBy conditions are `project`,<br>        `release`, `environment` and `session.status`.|
|orderBy|query|string|false|An optional field to order by, which must be one of the fields provided in `field`. Use `-`<br>        for descending order, for example, `-sum(session)`|
|includeTotals|query|integer|false|Specify `0` to exclude totals from the response. The default is `1`|
|includeSeries|query|integer|false|Specify `0` to exclude series from the response. The default is `1`|
|query|query|string|false|Filters results by using [query syntax](/product/sentry-basics/search/).<br><br>Example: `query=(transaction:foo AND release:abc) OR (transaction:[bar,baz] AND release:def)`<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "groups": [
    {
      "by": {
        "session.status": "errored"
      },
      "totals": {
        "sum(session)": 1000
      },
      "series": {
        "sum(session)": [
          368,
          392,
          240
        ]
      }
    },
    {
      "by": {
        "session.status": "healthy"
      },
      "totals": {
        "sum(session)": 17905998
      },
      "series": {
        "sum(session)": [
          6230841,
          6923689,
          4751465
        ]
      }
    }
  ],
  "start": "2024-01-29T07:30:00Z",
  "end": "2024-01-29T09:00:00Z",
  "intervals": [
    "2024-01-29T07:30:00Z",
    "2024-01-29T08:00:00Z",
    "2024-01-29T08:30:00Z"
  ],
  "query": ""
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-release-health-session-statistics-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|

<h3 id="retrieve-release-health-session-statistics-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|start|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|end|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|intervals|[string]|true|none|none|
|groups|[object]|true|none|none|
|» by|object|true|none|none|
|» » project|integer|false|none|none|
|» » release|string|false|none|none|
|» » environment|string|false|none|none|
|» » session.status|string|false|none|none|
|» series|object|true|none|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|[number(double) \| null]|false|none|none|
|» totals|object|true|none|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|number(double) \| null|false|none|none|
|query|string|true|none|none|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
auth_token
</aside>
````````````````````````````````````````````````````````
