`````````````````````````````````````````
## Upload a New Project Release File

<a id="opIduploadProjectReleaseFile"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/projects/string/string/releases/string/files/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'file=http://example.com' \
  -F 'name=string' \
  -F 'dist=string' \
  -F 'header=["string"]'
```

`POST /api/0/projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/releases/{version}/files/`

Upload a new file for the given release.

Files must be uploaded using the `multipart/form-data` content type, against the
region-specific domain (e.g. `us.sentry.io` or `de.sentry.io`).

> Body parameter

```yaml
file: "http://example.com"
name: string
dist: string
header:
  - string
```

<h3 id="upload-a-new-project-release-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|version|path|string|true|The version identifier of the release|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» file|body|string(uri)|true|The multipart-encoded file contents to upload.|
|» name|body|string|false|The name (full path) the file will be referenced as, e.g. the full web URI of a JavaScript file. Defaults to the uploaded file's name.|
|» dist|body|string|false|The name of the distribution to associate the file with.|
|» header|body|[string]|false|Headers to attach to the file, each formatted as a `"key:value"` string (for example, to define a content type). May be supplied multiple times.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "dist": "string",
  "headers": {
    "property1": null,
    "property2": null
  },
  "size": 0,
  "sha1": "string",
  "dateCreated": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="upload-a-new-project-release-file-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|
|409|Conflict|Conflict|None|

<h3 id="upload-a-new-project-release-file-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **201**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|none|
|name|string|true|none|none|
|dist|string \| null|true|none|none|
|headers|object|true|none|none|
|» **additionalProperties**|object|false|none|none|
|size|integer|true|none|none|
|sha1|string|true|none|none|
|dateCreated|string(date-time)|true|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
auth_token
</aside>

## Retrieve a Project's Release Setup Progress

<a id="opIdgetProjectReleaseSetupCompletion"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/projects/string/string/releases/completion/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/releases/completion/`

Return the project's release-setup progress for these steps:

- `tag`: The project has an issue with a recorded first release.
- `repo`: The organization has at least one repository.
- `commit`: At least one of the project's 1,000 most recent releases (by release ID) has an associated commit.
- `deploy`: At least one of the project's releases has a deploy.

Results are cached for one hour when a step is complete and one minute otherwise.

<h3 id="retrieve-a-projects-release-setup-progress-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "step": "tag",
    "complete": true
  }
]
```

<h3 id="retrieve-a-projects-release-setup-progress-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<h3 id="retrieve-a-projects-release-setup-progress-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» step|string|true|none|none|
|» complete|boolean|true|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|» step|tag|
|» step|repo|
|» step|commit|
|» step|deploy|
````````````````````````````````````````````````````````

## List an Organization's Installed Sentry App Components

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationSentryAppComponents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/sentry-app-components/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/sentry-app-components/`

**Experimental:** This API is under active development and may change.

Retrieve prepared UI components for installed custom integrations, including issue-link forms.

API clients can use `filter=issue-link` to create or link an external issue through
an app such as Linear. The `uri` values in `schema` are paths on the app's own server.
Clients never call them directly; Sentry calls the app on their behalf:

- To load a select field's choices, pass the field's `uri` to
  `GET /sentry-app-installations/{installationUuid}/external-requests/`.
- To create or link the issue, send the form values with the `uri` from
  `schema.create` or `schema.link` to
  `POST /sentry-app-installations/{installationUuid}/external-issue-actions/`.

<h3 id="list-an-organizations-installed-sentry-app-components-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|
|filter|query|string|false|Filter components by type, such as `issue-link`.|

## Create or Link an External Issue Through a Sentry App

<a id="opIdexecuteSentryAppInstallationExternalIssueAction"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/sentry-app-installations/string/external-issue-actions/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "groupId": "string",
    "action": "link",
    "uri": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /api/0/sentry-app-installations/{uuid}/external-issue-actions/`

**Experimental:** This API is under active development and may change.

Invoke the installed app's issue-link callback and store the returned association.
Submit the app-specific form fields alongside `groupId`, `action`, and `uri`.
The installation UUID, form fields, and `uri` come from the organization's
`issue-link` Sentry App components.

For `action=link`, the optional `expectedExternalIssueUrl` query parameter
requires an exact canonical `webUrl` match. An existing matching link is
returned with HTTP 200 without calling the App; a different link
returns 409. The callback must also return this URL before a new link is
saved. Callback effects cannot be rolled back if its response conflicts.
A new association returns HTTP 201. Omitting the parameter preserves the
App's existing replacement behavior and HTTP 200 response.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "groupId": "string",
  "action": "link",
  "uri": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-link-an-external-issue-through-a-sentry-app-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|uuid|path|string|true|The UUID of the Sentry App installation.|
|expectedExternalIssueUrl|query|string(uri)|false|The exact canonical webUrl of the external issue to link. Only supported for action=link. An existing matching association is a no-op; a different association or callback URL returns 409 without replacing the link.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» groupId|body|string|true|The numeric Sentry issue ID.|
|» action|body|string|true|The action to perform: `link` or `create`.|
|» uri|body|string|true|The relative callback URI from the app's issue-link form.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» action|link|
|» action|create|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "issueId": "string",
  "serviceType": "string",
  "displayName": "string",
  "webUrl": "string"
}
```

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "issueId": "string",
  "serviceType": "string",
  "displayName": "string",
  "webUrl": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-link-an-external-issue-through-a-sentry-app-responses">Responses</h3>

|200|OK||Inline|

|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|

|query|query|string|false|The search text for select options.|
|dependentData|query|string|false|A JSON-encoded object containing the values of fields this select depends on.|

|» webhookHeaders|body|[string]|false|Custom headers sent with every webhook request. Each entry is a single 'Header-Name: value' pair.|

## Retrieve an Integration's Issue Config for an Issue

<a id="opIdRetrieve an Integration's Issue Config for an Issue"></a>

> Code samples


`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/issues/{issue_id}/integrations/{integration_id}/`

Retrieve the form fields needed to either link an existing external issue
(such as a Jira ticket or GitHub issue) to a Sentry issue, or create a new
one. The returned `linkIssueConfig`/`createIssueConfig` describes the fields
to submit back to this endpoint via `PUT`/`POST` respectively.

|issue_id|path|string|true|The ID of the issue you'd like to query.|
|integration_id|path|string|true|The ID of the integration installed on the organization.|
|action|query|string|true|Whether to fetch the config for linking an existing external issue (`link`) or creating a new one (`create`).|

#### Enumerated Values

|---|---|
|action|create|
|action|link|

## Link an Existing External Issue to an Issue

<a id="opIdLink an Existing External Issue to an Issue"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/issues/string/integrations/string/' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "externalIssue": "string",
    "repo": "string",
    "comment": "string"
  }'
```

`PUT /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/issues/{issue_id}/integrations/{integration_id}/`

Link an issue that already exists in the external provider (such as a Jira
ticket or GitHub issue) to the given Sentry issue. Additional accepted fields
are integration-specific; fetch them from the `linkIssueConfig` returned by
the `GET` endpoint with `?action=link`. Linking the same issue again returns
the existing link with HTTP 200, without repeating provider comments. A new
link returns HTTP 201.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "externalIssue": "string",
  "repo": "string",
  "comment": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="link-an-existing-external-issue-to-an-issue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|issue_id|path|string|true|The ID of the issue you'd like to query.|
|integration_id|path|string|true|The ID of the integration installed on the organization.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» externalIssue|body|string|true|The identifier or full URL of the existing external issue to link. URL support depends on the selected integration.|
|» repo|body|string|false|The repository containing the external issue, in owner/name format. Required by GitHub, GitHub Enterprise, and Bitbucket integrations.|
|» comment|body|string|false|An optional comment to post to the external issue when linking, if supported by the integration.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": 0,
  "key": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "integrationId": 0,
  "displayName": "string"
}
```

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": 5,
  "key": "PROJECT-123",
  "url": "https://example.atlassian.net/browse/PROJECT-123",
  "integrationId": 123456,
  "displayName": "PROJECT-123"
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "detail": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="link-an-existing-external-issue-to-an-issue-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|201|Created||Inline|

|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|
|409|Conflict||Inline|

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

## Unlink an External Issue from an Issue

<a id="opIdUnlink an External Issue from an Issue"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/issues/string/integrations/string/?externalIssue=0' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/issues/{issue_id}/integrations/{integration_id}/`

Remove the link between a Sentry issue and an external issue. If no other
Sentry issues reference the external issue, the link record is deleted
entirely. An absent link also returns 204. This does not delete the issue
in the external provider.

<h3 id="unlink-an-external-issue-from-an-issue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|issue_id|path|string|true|The ID of the issue you'd like to query.|
|integration_id|path|string|true|The ID of the integration installed on the organization.|
|externalIssue|query|integer|true|The ID of the `ExternalIssue` link to remove.|

> Example responses

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "detail": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="unlink-an-external-issue-from-an-issue-responses">Responses</h3>

|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|No Content|None|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|

|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<h3 id="unlink-an-external-issue-from-an-issue-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **409**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|detail|string|true|none|none|

auth_token
</aside>

<h1 id="api-reference-scim">SCIM</h1>

System for Cross-Domain Identity Management ([SCIM](http://www.simplecloud.info/)) is a standard implemented by Identity Providers and applications in order to facilitate federated identity management. Through these APIs you can add and delete members as well as teams, and look up which SCIM features, resource types, and schemas Sentry supports. Sentry SaaS customers must be on a Business Plan with SAML2 Enabled. SCIM uses a bearer token for authentication that is created when SCIM is enabled. For how to enable SCIM, see our docs [here](/organization/authentication/sso/#scim-provisioning).
 Sentry's SCIM API does not currently support syncing passwords, or setting any User attributes other than `active`.

<a href="https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-docs/issues/new/?title=API%20Documentation%20Error:%20/api/integration-platform/&amp;template=api_error_template.md">Found an error? Let us know.</a>

## List an Organization's Paginated Teams

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationScimV2Groups"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/scim/v2/Groups' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/scim/v2/Groups`

Returns a paginated list of teams bound to a organization with a SCIM Groups GET Request.

Note that the members field will only contain up to 10,000 members.

<h3 id="list-an-organizations-paginated-teams-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|startIndex|query|integer|false|SCIM 1-offset based index for pagination.|
|count|query|integer|false|The maximum number of results the query should return, maximum of 100.|
|filter|query|string|false|A SCIM filter expression. The only operator currently supported is `eq`.|
|excludedAttributes|query|[string]|false|Fields that should be left off of return values. Right now the only supported field for this query is members.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "schemas": [
    "urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:ListResponse"
  ],
  "totalResults": 1,
  "startIndex": 1,
  "itemsPerPage": 1,
  "Resources": [
    {
      "schemas": [
        "urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:Group"
      ],
      "id": "23232",
      "displayName": "test-scimv2",
      "members": [],
      "meta": {
        "resourceType": "Group"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

|body|body|object|true|none|
|» schemas|body|[string]|true|SCIM schema URIs identifying the request format. Must be the PatchOp schema.|

Valid operations are:<br>* Renaming a team:<br>```json<br>{<br>    "Operations": [{<br>        "op": "replace",<br>        "value": {<br>            "id": 23,<br>            "displayName": "newName"<br>        }<br>    }]<br>}<br>```<br>* Adding a member to a team:<br>```json<br>{<br>    "Operations": [{<br>        "op": "add",<br>        "path": "members",<br>        "value": [<br>            {<br>                "value": 23,<br>                "display": "testexample@example.com"<br>            }<br>        ]<br>    }]<br>}<br>```<br>* Removing a member from a team:<br>```json<br>{<br>    "Operations": [{<br>        "op": "remove",<br>        "path": "members[value eq "23"]"<br>    }]<br>}<br>```<br>* Replacing an entire member set of a team:<br>```json<br>{<br>    "Operations": [{<br>        "op": "replace",<br>        "path": "members",<br>        "value": [<br>            {<br>                "value": 23,<br>                "display": "testexample2@sentry.io"<br>            },<br>            {<br>                "value": 24,<br>                "display": "testexample3@sentry.io"<br>            }<br>        ]<br>    }]<br>}<br>```<br>|
|» » op|body|string|true|none|

## Provision a New Organization Member

<a id="opIdprovisionOrganizationScimV2User"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/scim/v2/Users' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "userName": "user@example.com",
    "sentryOrgRole": "billing"
  }'
```

`POST /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/scim/v2/Users`

Create a new Organization Member via a SCIM Users POST Request.

Note that this API does not support setting secondary emails.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "userName": "user@example.com",
  "sentryOrgRole": "billing"
}
```

<h3 id="provision-a-new-organization-member-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» userName|body|string(email)|true|The SAML field used for email.|
|» sentryOrgRole|body|string|false|The organization role of the member. If unspecified, this will be<br>                    set to the organization's default role. The options are:<br><br>* `billing` - Can manage payment and compliance details.<br>* `member` - Can view and act on events, as well as view most other data within the organization.<br>* `manager` - Has full management access to all teams and projects. Can also manage<br>        the organization's membership.<br>* `admin` - Can edit global integrations, manage projects, and add/remove teams.<br>        They automatically assume the Team Admin role for teams they join.<br>        Note: This role can no longer be assigned in Business and Enterprise plans. Use `TeamRoles` instead.<br>        |

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» sentryOrgRole|billing|
|» sentryOrgRole|member|
|» sentryOrgRole|manager|
|» sentryOrgRole|admin|

```json
    "familyName": "N/A",
    "givenName": "N/A"
  },
  "meta": {
    "resourceType": "User"
  },
  "sentryOrgRole": "member"
}
```

```json
  ],
```

```bash
  "interval": "string"
```


<h3 id="create-a-new-saved-query-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The user-defined saved query name.|
|» projects|body|[integer]|false|The saved projects filter for this query.|
|» queryDataset|body|string|false|The dataset you would like to query. Note: `discover` is a **deprecated** value. The allowed values are: `error-events`, `transaction-like`<br><br>* `discover`<br>* `error-events`<br>* `transaction-like`|
|» start|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|The saved start time for this saved query.|
|» end|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|The saved end time for this saved query.|
|» range|body|string \| null|false|The saved time range period for this saved query.|
|» fields|body|[string]|false|The fields, functions, or equations that can be requested for the query. At most 20 fields can be selected per request. Each field can be one of the following types:<br>- A built-in key field. See possible fields in the [properties table](/product/sentry-basics/search/searchable-properties/#properties-table), under any field that is an event property.<br>    - example: `field=transaction`<br>- A tag. Tags should use the `tag[]` formatting to avoid ambiguity with any fields<br>    - example: `field=tag[isEnterprise]`<br>- A function which will be in the format of `function_name(parameters,...)`. See possible functions in the [query builder documentation](/product/discover-queries/query-builder/#stacking-functions).<br>    - when a function is included, Discover will group by any tags or fields<br>    - example: `field=count_if(transaction.duration,greater,300)`<br>- An equation when prefixed with `equation\|`. Read more about [equations here](/product/discover-queries/query-builder/query-equations/).<br>    - example: `field=equation\|count_if(transaction.duration,greater,300) / count() * 100`<br>|
|» orderby|body|string \| null|false|How to order the query results. Must be something in the `field` list, excluding equations.|
|» rollup|body|integer \| null|false|Time-bucket granularity in seconds for the saved query.|
|» aggregations|body|[[object]]|false|Aggregate functions to apply, each as a `[function, column, alias]` triple.|
|» groupby|body|[string]|false|Columns to group results by.|
|» conditions|body|[[object]]|false|Filter conditions, each as a `[column, operator, value]` triple.|
|» limit|body|integer \| null|false|Maximum number of rows to return, from `0` to `1000`.|
|» version|body|integer \| null|false|Saved query schema version. `1` for the legacy shape, `2` for the current one.|
|» environment|body|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|
|» query|body|string \| null|false|Filters results by using [query syntax](/product/sentry-basics/search/).|
|» widths|body|[string]|false|Rendered column widths, in the same order as the query's fields.|
|» yAxis|body|[string]|false|Aggregate functions to be plotted on the chart.|
|» display|body|string \| null|false|Visualization type for saved query chart. Allowed values are:<br>- default<br>- previous<br>- top5<br>- daily<br>- dailytop5<br>- bar<br>|
|» topEvents|body|integer \| null|false|Number of top events' timeseries to be visualized.|
|» interval|body|string \| null|false|Resolution of the time series.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» queryDataset|discover|
|» queryDataset|error-events|
|» queryDataset|transaction-like|

<h3 id="edit-an-organizations-discover-saved-query-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|query_id|path|integer|true|The ID of the Discover query you'd like to retrieve.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The user-defined saved query name.|
|» projects|body|[integer]|false|The saved projects filter for this query.|
|» queryDataset|body|string|false|The dataset you would like to query. Note: `discover` is a **deprecated** value. The allowed values are: `error-events`, `transaction-like`<br><br>* `discover`<br>* `error-events`<br>* `transaction-like`|
|» start|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|The saved start time for this saved query.|
|» end|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|The saved end time for this saved query.|
|» range|body|string \| null|false|The saved time range period for this saved query.|
|» fields|body|[string]|false|The fields, functions, or equations that can be requested for the query. At most 20 fields can be selected per request. Each field can be one of the following types:<br>- A built-in key field. See possible fields in the [properties table](/product/sentry-basics/search/searchable-properties/#properties-table), under any field that is an event property.<br>    - example: `field=transaction`<br>- A tag. Tags should use the `tag[]` formatting to avoid ambiguity with any fields<br>    - example: `field=tag[isEnterprise]`<br>- A function which will be in the format of `function_name(parameters,...)`. See possible functions in the [query builder documentation](/product/discover-queries/query-builder/#stacking-functions).<br>    - when a function is included, Discover will group by any tags or fields<br>    - example: `field=count_if(transaction.duration,greater,300)`<br>- An equation when prefixed with `equation\|`. Read more about [equations here](/product/discover-queries/query-builder/query-equations/).<br>    - example: `field=equation\|count_if(transaction.duration,greater,300) / count() * 100`<br>|
|» orderby|body|string \| null|false|How to order the query results. Must be something in the `field` list, excluding equations.|
|» rollup|body|integer \| null|false|Time-bucket granularity in seconds for the saved query.|
|» aggregations|body|[[object]]|false|Aggregate functions to apply, each as a `[function, column, alias]` triple.|
|» groupby|body|[string]|false|Columns to group results by.|
|» conditions|body|[[object]]|false|Filter conditions, each as a `[column, operator, value]` triple.|
|» limit|body|integer \| null|false|Maximum number of rows to return, from `0` to `1000`.|
|» version|body|integer \| null|false|Saved query schema version. `1` for the legacy shape, `2` for the current one.|
|» environment|body|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|
|» query|body|string \| null|false|Filters results by using [query syntax](/product/sentry-basics/search/).|
|» widths|body|[string]|false|Rendered column widths, in the same order as the query's fields.|
|» yAxis|body|[string]|false|Aggregate functions to be plotted on the chart.|
|» display|body|string \| null|false|Visualization type for saved query chart. Allowed values are:<br>- default<br>- previous<br>- top5<br>- daily<br>- dailytop5<br>- bar<br>|
|» topEvents|body|integer \| null|false|Number of top events' timeseries to be visualized.|
|» interval|body|string \| null|false|Resolution of the time series.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» queryDataset|discover|
|» queryDataset|error-events|
|» queryDataset|transaction-like|

## List an Organization's Tags

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationTags"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/tags/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/tags/`

Return a list of tag keys for the given organization.

<h3 id="list-an-organizations-tags-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project|query|[integer \| string]|false|The IDs or slugs of projects to filter by. Project slugs are unique within each organization. Omit this parameter to include all accessible projects. `-1` is also accepted to include all accessible projects.<br>For example, the following are valid parameters:<br>- `/?project=1234&project=56789`<br>- `/?project=android&project=javascript-react`<br>- `/?project=-1`<br>|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time for the query, will override the start & end parameters, a number followed by one of:<br>- `d` for days<br>- `h` for hours<br>- `m` for minutes<br>- `s` for seconds<br>- `w` for weeks<br><br>For example, `24h`, to mean query data starting from 24 hours ago to now.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|dataset|query|string|false|The dataset to query. Defaults to `discover`.|
|use_cache|query|string|false|Set to `"1"` to enable caching for the tag key query.|
|useFlagsBackend|query|string|false|Set to `"1"` to query feature flags instead of tags.|

#### Enumerated Values

|dataset|discover|
|dataset|events|
|dataset|replays|

|use_cache|0|
|use_cache|1|
|useFlagsBackend|0|
|useFlagsBackend|1|

## List Trace Item Attributes

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationTraceItemAttributes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/trace-items/attributes/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/trace-items/attributes/`

List the attribute keys available on a given trace item dataset (spans, logs,
trace metrics, etc.), with optional substring and structured filtering.

Pass `expand=context` (experimental) to include each attribute's metadata:
a brief description, examples, and deprecation details.

<h3 id="list-trace-item-attributes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time for the query, will override the start & end parameters, a number followed by one of:<br>- `d` for days<br>- `h` for hours<br>- `m` for minutes<br>- `s` for seconds<br>- `w` for weeks<br><br>For example, `24h`, to mean query data starting from 24 hours ago to now.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|
|project|query|[integer \| string]|false|The IDs or slugs of projects to filter by. Project slugs are unique within each organization. Omit this parameter to include all accessible projects. `-1` is also accepted to include all accessible projects.<br>For example, the following are valid parameters:<br>- `/?project=1234&project=56789`<br>- `/?project=android&project=javascript-react`<br>- `/?project=-1`<br>|
|dataset|query|string|false|The trace item dataset to list attributes for. One of `itemType` or `dataset` is required.|
|itemType|query|string|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated alias of `dataset`. Use `dataset` instead.|
|attributeType|query|[string]|false|Filter to attributes of one or more types. Defaults to all types.|

## Retrieve Trace Metadata

<a id="opIdgetOrganizationTraceMeta"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/trace-meta/string/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/trace-meta/{trace_id}/`

Retrieve aggregate metadata for a single trace, including counts of spans,
errors, performance issues, logs, and metrics, along with per-span-operation
and per-transaction child-count breakdowns.

<h3 id="retrieve-trace-metadata-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|trace_id|path|string|true|The ID of the trace, a 32-character hexadecimal string.|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time for the query, will override the start & end parameters, a number followed by one of:<br>- `d` for days<br>- `h` for hours<br>- `m` for minutes<br>- `s` for seconds<br>- `w` for weeks<br><br>For example, `24h`, to mean query data starting from 24 hours ago to now.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|include_uptime|query|string|false|Set to `1` to include uptime check counts in the response. Defaults to `0` (disabled).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|include_uptime|0|
|include_uptime|1|

## Retrieve a Trace

<a id="opIdgetOrganizationTrace"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/trace/string/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/trace/{trace_id}/`

Retrieve the spans, errors, and (optionally) uptime checks that make up a single trace.

The response is a list of top-level events; each item may have nested `children`, `errors`,
and `occurrences` arrays representing related items. Top-level entries are spans by default
and may also be uptime checks when `include_uptime=1` is passed.

<h3 id="retrieve-a-trace-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|trace_id|path|string|true|The ID of the trace, a 32-character hexadecimal string.|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time for the query, will override the start & end parameters, a number followed by one of:<br>- `d` for days<br>- `h` for hours<br>- `m` for minutes<br>- `s` for seconds<br>- `w` for weeks<br><br>For example, `24h`, to mean query data starting from 24 hours ago to now.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|referrer|query|string|false|Internal referrer identifier used for query tracing. Most clients can omit this.|
|errorId|query|string|false|A 32-character hexadecimal event ID to bias the trace results toward including.|
|additional_attributes|query|[string]|false|Additional span attributes to include on each event. Repeat to request multiple.|
|include_uptime|query|string|false|Set to `1` to include uptime check results in the trace. Defaults to `0`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|include_uptime|0|
|include_uptime|1|

## List an Organization's AI Conversations

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationAIConversations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/agents/conversations/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/agents/conversations/`

**Experimental:** This API is under active development and may change.

Return AI conversations ordered by latest span time.

`query` uses Sentry search syntax.

**Span filters**

- Description: `"payment failed"`; status: `span.status:[error,internal_error]`.
- Operation: `gen_ai.operation.type:tool`; tool: `gen_ai.tool.name:get_weather`.
- Duration: `span.duration:>2s`; ID: `gen_ai.conversation.id:"session:123"`
  or `conversation.conversationId:"session:123"`.

**Conversation filters**

- Calls: `conversation.llmCalls` or `conversation.messages`, and
  `conversation.toolCalls`; failures: `conversation.errors` and
  `conversation.toolErrors`.
- Usage: `conversation.inputTokens`, `conversation.outputTokens`,
  `conversation.totalTokens`, and `conversation.totalCost`.
- Timespan: `conversation.timeSpan` measures elapsed time between first and last AI spans;
  `conversation.generationDuration` sums LLM call durations. Both use milliseconds.

Use numeric comparisons such as `conversation.toolCalls:>2`. Queries return
conversations, not spans. Each `AND` condition may match a different span.
Returned totals include all AI spans in selected project, environment, and time
filters, not only matching spans.

Negation means no span matches, including when an attribute is absent. Payloads
are searchable only when recorded and not scrubbed. Payload failure text does
not mark a span as failed; set `span.status:error` for reliable failure search.

<h3 id="list-an-organizations-ai-conversations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project|query|[integer \| string]|false|The IDs or slugs of projects to filter by. Project slugs are unique within each organization. Omit this parameter to include all accessible projects. `-1` is also accepted to include all accessible projects.<br>For example, the following are valid parameters:<br>- `/?project=1234&project=56789`<br>- `/?project=android&project=javascript-react`<br>- `/?project=-1`<br>|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time for the query, will override the start & end parameters, a number followed by one of:<br>- `d` for days<br>- `h` for hours<br>- `m` for minutes<br>- `s` for seconds<br>- `w` for weeks<br><br>For example, `24h`, to mean query data starting from 24 hours ago to now.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|query|query|string|false|Sentry search syntax matched against spans. A conversation is returned when any span in it matches. Summary fields include all spans in selected projects and time range, not only matching spans.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of conversations to return per page. Defaults to 10; maximum is 100.|

> 200 Response

```json

  {
    "conversationId": "01JQZ4W8X7J2Q9B4R5M6N7P8T9",
```

## Retrieve an Organization's AI Conversation

<a id="opIdretrieveOrganizationAIConversation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/agents/conversations/string/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/agents/conversations/{conversation_id}/`

**Experimental:** This API is under active development and may change.

Return spans recorded for one AI conversation in start-time order.

Message, tool, and response attributes contain their recorded string values.
`stats.errors` counts spans whose status is not `ok`, `cancelled`, or `unknown`.
`stats.errorToolNames` lists tools used by those spans.
`stats.inputTokens` includes cache-read and cache-write tokens. In `stats.usageByModel`,
`inputCost` includes cache-read and cache-write costs, and `outputCost` includes
reasoning cost. These cost breakdowns are not added to `totalCost`.
Stats are returned on the first page only. Without an explicit range, Sentry widens
the search across available retention. A missing conversation returns an empty `spans` list.

<h3 id="retrieve-an-organizations-ai-conversation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|conversation_id|path|string|true|Conversation ID recorded in `gen_ai.conversation.id`.|
|project|query|[integer \| string]|false|The IDs or slugs of projects to filter by. Project slugs are unique within each organization. Omit this parameter to include all accessible projects. `-1` is also accepted to include all accessible projects.<br>For example, the following are valid parameters:<br>- `/?project=1234&project=56789`<br>- `/?project=android&project=javascript-react`<br>- `/?project=-1`<br>|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time for the query, will override the start & end parameters, a number followed by one of:<br>- `d` for days<br>- `h` for hours<br>- `m` for minutes<br>- `s` for seconds<br>- `w` for weeks<br><br>For example, `24h`, to mean query data starting from 24 hours ago to now.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of spans to return per page. Defaults to 100; maximum is 1,000.|
|view|query|string|false|Defaults to timeline (paginated raw spans). Transcript returns paginated normalized messages; requires feature access. Transcript timestamps and durations are seconds.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|view|timeline|
|view|transcript|

## Query Explore Events in Table Format

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/events/?field=string&dataset=errors' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/events/`

Retrieves explore data for a given organization.

**Note**: This endpoint is intended to get a table of results, and is not for doing a full export of data sent to
Sentry.

The `field` query parameter determines what fields will be selected in the `data` and `meta` keys of the endpoint response.
- The `data` key contains a list of results row by row that match the `query` made
- The `meta` key contains information about the response, including the unit or type of the fields requested
- EAP table results may include `meta.routingHint`. Pass this opaque value unchanged as
  `routing_hint` when fetching item details for a row in this response. It identifies how
  the table query was routed and is omitted when no hint is available.

<h3 id="query-explore-events-in-table-format-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|field|query|[string]|true|The fields, functions, or equations to request for the query. At most 20 fields can be selected per request. Each field can be one of the following types:<br>- A built-in key field. See possible fields in the [properties table](/concepts/search/searchable-properties/), under any field that matches the dataset passed to the dataset parameter<br>    - example: `field=transaction`<br>- A tag. Tags should use the `tag[{name}, {type}]` formatting to avoid ambiguity with any fields,<br>    - example: `field=tag[isEnterprise, string]`<br>    - example: `field=tag[numberOfBytes, number]`<br>- A function which will be in the format of `function_name(parameters,...)`. See possible functions in the [query builder documentation](/product/discover-queries/query-builder/#stacking-functions).<br>    - when a function is included, Discover will group by any tags or fields<br>    - example: `field=count_if(transaction.duration,greater,300)`<br>- An equation when prefixed with `equation\|`. Read more about [equations here](/product/discover-queries/query-builder/query-equations/).<br>    - example: `field=equation\|count_if(transaction.duration,greater,300) / count() * 100`<br>|
|dataset|query|string|true|Which dataset to query. The chosen dataset determines which fields are queryable.<br>- `errors` - Error events.<br>- `logs` - Structured log events.<br>- `profile_functions` - Function-level Profiling data.<br>- `spans` - Distributed tracing span events.<br>- `tracemetrics` - Application Metrics.<br>- `uptime_results` - Uptime monitoring check results.<br>|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|
|referrer|query|string|false|Internal referrer identifier used for query tracing. Most clients can omit this.|
|project|query|[integer \| string]|false|The IDs or slugs of projects to filter by. Project slugs are unique within each organization. Omit this parameter to include all accessible projects. `-1` is also accepted to include all accessible projects.<br>For example, the following are valid parameters:<br>- `/?project=1234&project=56789`<br>- `/?project=android&project=javascript-react`<br>- `/?project=-1`<br>|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time for the query, will override the start & end parameters, a number followed by one of:<br>- `d` for days<br>- `h` for hours<br>- `m` for minutes<br>- `s` for seconds<br>- `w` for weeks<br><br>For example, `24h`, to mean query data starting from 24 hours ago to now.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Limit the number of rows to return in the result. Default and maximum allowed is 100.|
|query|query|string|false|Filters results by using [query syntax](/concepts/search/).<br><br>Example: `query=(transaction:foo AND release:abc) OR (transaction:[bar,baz] AND release:def)`<br><br>With the `logs` dataset, a string attribute can also be matched against a regular expression written as `key://pattern//`, and excluded with `!key://pattern//`.<br>Patterns use [RE2 syntax](https://github.com/google/re2/wiki/Syntax), match anywhere in the value unless anchored with `^` or `$`, are case sensitive unless they start with `(?i)`, and are limited to 64 characters. A query can contain up to 16 regular expressions.<br>To search for a literal value that starts with `//`, quote it: `key:"//value"`.<br>See [regular expressions](/concepts/search/#regular-expressions-logs-only) for more details.<br><br>Example: `query=message://^Timeout after \d+ms//`<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|What to order the results of the query by. Must be something in the `field` list, excluding equations.|
|allowAggregateConditions|query|boolean|false|If false, aggregate conditions in the query string are disallowed. Defaults to true.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|

#### Enumerated Values

|---|---|
|dataset|errors|
|dataset|logs|
|dataset|profile_functions|
|dataset|spans|
|dataset|tracemetrics|
|dataset|uptime_results|

## Query Dropped and Accepted Events/Stats by Outcome and Reason

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationEventsDropped"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/events-dropped/?dataset=errors' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/events-dropped/`

**Experimental:** This API is under active development and may change.

Return the events Sentry received but dropped (rate limited, filtered,
invalid, abuse, client discarded, cardinality limited) bucketed over the
requested interval, alongside the accepted volume per bucket so a caller
can compute the dropped share.

Select the dropped-data type with ``dataset`` and the bucket size with
``interval``. Optionally scope the dropped side to one classification with
``outcome`` (top-level) and/or ``reason`` (sub-classification within an
outcome); the accepted volume is always returned in full.

<h3 id="query-dropped-and-accepted-eventsstats-by-outcome-and-reason-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|dataset|query|string|true|Which dataset to query. The chosen dataset determines which fields are queryable.<br>- `errors` - Error events.<br>- `logs` - Structured log events.<br>- `profile_functions` - Function-level Profiling data.<br>- `spans` - Distributed tracing span events.<br>- `tracemetrics` - Application Metrics.<br>- `uptime_results` - Uptime monitoring check results.<br>|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|
|project|query|[integer \| string]|false|The IDs or slugs of projects to filter by. Project slugs are unique within each organization. Omit this parameter to include all accessible projects. `-1` is also accepted to include all accessible projects.<br>For example, the following are valid parameters:<br>- `/?project=1234&project=56789`<br>- `/?project=android&project=javascript-react`<br>- `/?project=-1`<br>|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time for the query, will override the start & end parameters, a number followed by one of:<br>- `d` for days<br>- `h` for hours<br>- `m` for minutes<br>- `s` for seconds<br>- `w` for weeks<br><br>For example, `24h`, to mean query data starting from 24 hours ago to now.|
|interval|query|integer|false|The size of the bucket for the timeseries to have, must be a value smaller than the window being<br>queried. If the interval is invalid a default interval will be selected instead|
|outcome|query|string|false|Narrow the dropped events (only) to a single top-level drop classification (e.g. `rate_limited`, `filtered`).<br><br>* `filtered`<br>* `rate_limited`<br>* `invalid`<br>* `abuse`<br>* `client_discard`<br>* `cardinality_limited`|
|reason|query|string|false|Narrow the dropped events to a single reason, the sub-classification within an outcome (e.g. `spike_protection` within `rate_limited`). Should be combined with `outcome`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|dataset|errors|
|dataset|logs|
|dataset|profile_functions|
|dataset|spans|
|dataset|tracemetrics|
|dataset|uptime_results|
|outcome|filtered|
|outcome|rate_limited|
|outcome|invalid|
|outcome|abuse|
|outcome|client_discard|
|outcome|cardinality_limited|

## Query Explore Events in Timeseries Format

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationEventsTimeseries"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/events-timeseries/?dataset=errors' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/events-timeseries/`

Retrieves explore data for a given organization as a timeseries.

This endpoint can return timeseries for either 1 or many axis, and results grouped to the top events depending
on the parameters passed

**Note**: For queries extending past `30d`, spanning billions of rows, or running on projects with low
sample rates, the aggregation `yAxis=count_unique()` and filters on high-cardinality
fields (such as `query=user.id:bc`) will not return accurate results. Use these queries for rough
estimation only.

<h3 id="query-explore-events-in-timeseries-format-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|dataset|query|string|true|Which dataset to query. The chosen dataset determines which fields are queryable.<br>- `errors` - Error events.<br>- `logs` - Structured log events.<br>- `profile_functions` - Function-level Profiling data.<br>- `spans` - Distributed tracing span events.<br>- `tracemetrics` - Application Metrics.<br>- `uptime_results` - Uptime monitoring check results.<br>|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|
|project|query|[integer \| string]|false|The IDs or slugs of projects to filter by. Project slugs are unique within each organization. Omit this parameter to include all accessible projects. `-1` is also accepted to include all accessible projects.<br>For example, the following are valid parameters:<br>- `/?project=1234&project=56789`<br>- `/?project=android&project=javascript-react`<br>- `/?project=-1`<br>|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time for the query, will override the start & end parameters, a number followed by one of:<br>- `d` for days<br>- `h` for hours<br>- `m` for minutes<br>- `s` for seconds<br>- `w` for weeks<br><br>For example, `24h`, to mean query data starting from 24 hours ago to now.|
|topEvents|query|integer|false|The number of top event results to return, must be between 1 and 10.<br>When TopEvents is passed, both sort and groupBy are required parameters|
|comparisonDelta|query|integer|false|The delta in seconds to return additional offset timeseries by|
|interval|query|integer|false|The size of the bucket for the timeseries to have, must be a value smaller than the window being<br>queried. If the interval is invalid a default interval will be selected instead|
|sort|query|string|false|What to order the results of the query by. Must be something in the `field` list, excluding equations.|
|groupBy|query|[string]|false|List of fields to group by, *Required* for topEvents queries as this and sort determine what the<br>top events are|
|yAxis|query|string|false|The aggregate field to create the timeseries for, defaults to `count()` when<br>        not included.<br>- `count()` - Total count of events over the period.<br>- `avg(field)` - Average value of the field over the period.<br>- `pXX(field)` - Percentile value of the field over the period. One of: `p50`, `p75`, `p90`, `p95`, `p99`, `p100`.<br>- `sum(field)` - Sum of all values for the field over the period.<br>- `min(field)` - Lowest value observed for the field over the period.<br>- `max(field)` - Highest value observed for the field over the period.<br>- `count_unique(field)` - Count of unique values observed for the field over the period. See *Note:* regarding accuracy on sampled data.<br>- `epm` - Average number of events received per minute.<br>- `eps` - Average number of events received per second.<br>- `failure_rate()` - Percentage of events whose `status` indicates failure.<br>- `failure_count()` - Total count of events with an error `status` over period.<br>- `performance_score(field)` - Web Vitals performance score for the selected measurement.<br>- `opportunity_score(field)` - Web Vitals opportunity score for the selected measurement.<br>|
|query|query|string|false|Filters results by using [query syntax](/concepts/search/).<br><br>Example: `query=(transaction:foo AND release:abc) OR (transaction:[bar,baz] AND release:def)`<br><br>With the `logs` dataset, a string attribute can also be matched against a regular expression written as `key://pattern//`, and excluded with `!key://pattern//`.<br>Patterns use [RE2 syntax](https://github.com/google/re2/wiki/Syntax), match anywhere in the value unless anchored with `^` or `$`, are case sensitive unless they start with `(?i)`, and are limited to 64 characters. A query can contain up to 16 regular expressions.<br>To search for a literal value that starts with `//`, quote it: `key:"//value"`.<br>See [regular expressions](/concepts/search/#regular-expressions-logs-only) for more details.<br><br>Example: `query=message://^Timeout after \d+ms//`<br>|
|disableAggregateExtrapolation|query|string|false|Whether to disable the use of extrapolation and return the sampled values, due to sampling the<br>number returned may be less than the actual values sent to Sentry|
|preventMetricAggregates|query|string|false|Whether to throw an error when aggregates are passed in the query or groupBy|
|excludeOther|query|string|false|Only applicable with TopEvents, whether to include the 'other' timeseries which represents all the<br>events that aren't in the top groups.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|dataset|errors|
|dataset|logs|
|dataset|profile_functions|
|dataset|spans|
|dataset|tracemetrics|
|dataset|uptime_results|
|disableAggregateExtrapolation|0|
|disableAggregateExtrapolation|1|
|preventMetricAggregates|0|
|preventMetricAggregates|1|
|excludeOther|0|
|excludeOther|1|

**Experimental:** This API is under active development and may change.

<h3 id="list-an-organizations-trace-metrics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|

Omit this parameter to include all accessible projects. `-1` is also accepted to include all accessible projects.<br>For example, the following are valid parameters:<br>- `/?project=1234&project=56789`<br>- `/?project=android&project=javascript-react`<br>- `/?project=-1`<br>|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time for the query, will override the start & end parameters, a number followed by one of:<br>- `d` for days<br>- `h` for hours<br>- `m` for minutes<br>- `s` for seconds<br>- `w` for weeks<br><br>For example, `24h`, to mean query data starting from 24 hours ago to now.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|query|query|string|false|Search query to filter metrics, using the same syntax as the metrics dataset.|
|sort|query|string|false|Response field to sort by, prefixed with `-` for descending. Defaults to metric name ascending.|

## Retrieve Trace Item Statistics

<a id="opIdRetrieve Trace Item Statistics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/trace-items/stats/?statsType=attributeDistributions' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/trace-items/stats/`

Compute statistics, such as attribute value distributions, over the trace
items (spans or occurrences) matching the given query within the requested
time range.

<h3 id="retrieve-trace-item-statistics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|statsType|query|[string]|true|The statistics to compute over the matching trace items.|
|project|query|[integer \| string]|false|The IDs or slugs of projects to filter by. Project slugs are unique within each organization. Omit this parameter to include all accessible projects. `-1` is also accepted to include all accessible projects.<br>For example, the following are valid parameters:<br>- `/?project=1234&project=56789`<br>- `/?project=android&project=javascript-react`<br>- `/?project=-1`<br>|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time for the query, will override the start & end parameters, a number followed by one of:<br>- `d` for days<br>- `h` for hours<br>- `m` for minutes<br>- `s` for seconds<br>- `w` for weeks<br><br>For example, `24h`, to mean query data starting from 24 hours ago to now.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|itemType|query|string|false|The trace item dataset to compute statistics for. Defaults to `spans`.|
|query|query|string|false|Sentry [search syntax](https://docs.sentry.io/concepts/search/) to filter trace items before computing statistics.|
|substringMatch|query|string|false|Restrict results to attribute names containing this substring (case-sensitive).|
|traceItemsLimit|query|integer|false|Maximum number of trace items to sample when computing statistics. Defaults to `1000`, which is also the maximum.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|

## List an Organization's Custom Dashboards

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationDashboards"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/dashboards/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/dashboards/`

Retrieve a list of custom dashboards that are associated with the given organization.

<h3 id="list-an-organizations-custom-dashboards-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|filter|query|[string]|false|Filter the dashboards returned. Repeat this parameter to apply multiple filters.|
|query|query|string|false|Filter dashboards by title.|
|sort|query|string|false|The property to sort results by. Prefix the value with `-` to sort in descending order.<br><br>Available fields are:<br>- `title`<br>- `dateCreated`<br>- `mostPopular`<br>- `recentlyViewed`<br>- `mydashboards`<br>- `myDashboardsAndRecentlyViewed`<br>|
|pin|query|string|false|Pin favorited dashboards to the top of the results.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Limit the number of rows to return in the result. Default and maximum allowed is 100.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|filter|excludeFavorites|
|filter|excludePrebuilt|
|filter|onlyFavorites|
|filter|onlyPrebuilt|
|filter|owned|
|filter|shared|
|filter|showHidden|
|pin|favorites|

## Retrieve Monitors for an Organization

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationMonitors"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/monitors/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/monitors/`

Lists monitors, including nested monitor environments. May be filtered to a project or environment.

<h3 id="retrieve-monitors-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project|query|[integer \| string]|false|The IDs or slugs of projects to filter by. Project slugs are unique within each organization. Omit this parameter to include all accessible projects. `-1` is also accepted to include all accessible projects.<br>For example, the following are valid parameters:<br>- `/?project=1234&project=56789`<br>- `/?project=android&project=javascript-react`<br>- `/?project=-1`<br>|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|
|owner|query|string|false|The owner of the monitor, in the format `user:id` or `team:id`. May be specified multiple times.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|

## Create a Monitor

<a id="opIdcreateOrganizationMonitor"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/monitors/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "project": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "config": {
      "schedule_type": "crontab",
      "schedule": null,
      "checkin_margin": 1,
      "max_runtime": 1,
      "timezone": "Africa/Abidjan",
      "failure_issue_threshold": 1,
      "recovery_threshold": 1
    },
    "slug": "string",
    "status": "active",
    "owner": "string",
    "is_muted": true
  }'
```

`POST /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/monitors/`

Create a new monitor.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "project": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "config": {
    "schedule_type": "crontab",
    "schedule": null,
    "checkin_margin": 1,
    "max_runtime": 1,
    "timezone": "Africa/Abidjan",
    "failure_issue_threshold": 1,
    "recovery_threshold": 1
  },
  "slug": "string",
  "status": "active",
  "owner": "string",
  "is_muted": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-monitor-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» project|body|string|true|The project ID or slug to associate the monitor to.|
|» name|body|string|true|Name of the monitor. Used for notifications. If not set the slug will be derived from your monitor name.|
|» config|body|object|true|The configuration for the monitor.|
|» » schedule_type|body|string|false|Currently supports "crontab" or "interval"<br><br>* `crontab`<br>* `interval`|
|» » schedule|body|object|true|Varies depending on the schedule_type. Is either a crontab string, or a 2 element tuple for intervals (e.g. [1, 'day'])|
|» » checkin_margin|body|integer \| null|false|How long (in minutes) after the expected checkin time will we wait until we consider the checkin to have been missed.|
|» » max_runtime|body|integer \| null|false|How long (in minutes) is the checkin allowed to run for in CheckInStatus.IN_PROGRESS before it is considered failed. Maximum 10080 (7 days).|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created||Inline|

|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<h3 id="create-a-monitor-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **201**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|none|
|name|string|true|none|none|
|slug|string|true|none|none|
|status|string|true|none|none|
|isMuted|boolean|true|none|none|
|isUpserting|boolean|true|none|none|
|config|object|true|none|none|
|» schedule_type|string|true|none|none|
|» schedule|string \| [integer]|true|none|none|
|» » *anyOf*|string|false|none|none|
|» » *anyOf*|[integer]|false|none|none|
|*anonymous*|[integer]|false|none|none|
|» checkin_margin|integer \| null|true|none|none|
|» max_runtime|integer \| null|true|none|none|

## Update a Monitor

<a id="opIdupdateOrganizationMonitor"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/monitors/string/' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "project": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "config": {
      "schedule_type": "crontab",
      "schedule": null,
      "checkin_margin": 1,
      "max_runtime": 1,
      "timezone": "Africa/Abidjan",
      "failure_issue_threshold": 1,
      "recovery_threshold": 1
    },
    "slug": "string",
    "status": "active",
    "owner": "string",
    "is_muted": true
  }'
```

`PUT /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/monitors/{monitor_id_or_slug}/`

Update a monitor.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "project": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "config": {
    "schedule_type": "crontab",
    "schedule": null,
    "checkin_margin": 1,
    "max_runtime": 1,
    "timezone": "Africa/Abidjan",
    "failure_issue_threshold": 1,
    "recovery_threshold": 1
  },
  "slug": "string",
  "status": "active",
  "owner": "string",
  "is_muted": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-monitor-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|monitor_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the monitor.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» project|body|string|true|The project ID or slug to associate the monitor to.|
|» name|body|string|true|Name of the monitor. Used for notifications. If not set the slug will be derived from your monitor name.|
|» config|body|object|true|The configuration for the monitor.|
|» » schedule_type|body|string|false|Currently supports "crontab" or "interval"<br><br>* `crontab`<br>* `interval`|
|» » schedule|body|object|true|Varies depending on the schedule_type. Is either a crontab string, or a 2 element tuple for intervals (e.g. [1, 'day'])|
|» » checkin_margin|body|integer \| null|false|How long (in minutes) after the expected checkin time will we wait until we consider the checkin to have been missed.|
|» » max_runtime|body|integer \| null|false|How long (in minutes) is the checkin allowed to run for in CheckInStatus.IN_PROGRESS before it is considered failed. Maximum 10080 (7 days).|

## Delete a Monitor or Monitor Environments

<a id="opIddeleteOrganizationMonitor"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/monitors/string/' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/monitors/{monitor_id_or_slug}/`

Delete a monitor or monitor environments.

<h3 id="delete-a-monitor-or-monitor-environments-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|monitor_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the monitor.|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|

<h3 id="delete-a-monitor-or-monitor-environments-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Accepted|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
auth_token
</aside>

## Retrieve Check-Ins for a Monitor

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationMonitorCheckins"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/organizations/string/monitors/string/checkins/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/monitors/{monitor_id_or_slug}/checkins/`

Retrieve a list of check-ins for a monitor

<h3 id="retrieve-check-ins-for-a-monitor-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|monitor_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the monitor.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|

## Update a Monitor for a Project

<a id="opIdupdateProjectMonitor"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/projects/string/string/monitors/string/' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "project": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "config": {
      "schedule_type": "crontab",
      "schedule": null,
      "checkin_margin": 1,
      "max_runtime": 1,
      "timezone": "Africa/Abidjan",
      "failure_issue_threshold": 1,
      "recovery_threshold": 1
    },
    "slug": "string",
    "status": "active",
    "owner": "string",
    "is_muted": true
  }'
```

`PUT /api/0/projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/monitors/{monitor_id_or_slug}/`

Update a monitor.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "project": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "config": {
    "schedule_type": "crontab",
    "schedule": null,
    "checkin_margin": 1,
    "max_runtime": 1,
    "timezone": "Africa/Abidjan",
    "failure_issue_threshold": 1,
    "recovery_threshold": 1
  },
  "slug": "string",
  "status": "active",
  "owner": "string",
  "is_muted": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-monitor-for-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|monitor_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the monitor.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» project|body|string|true|The project ID or slug to associate the monitor to.|
|» name|body|string|true|Name of the monitor. Used for notifications. If not set the slug will be derived from your monitor name.|
|» config|body|object|true|The configuration for the monitor.|
|» » schedule_type|body|string|false|Currently supports "crontab" or "interval"<br><br>* `crontab`<br>* `interval`|
|» » schedule|body|object|true|Varies depending on the schedule_type. Is either a crontab string, or a 2 element tuple for intervals (e.g. [1, 'day'])|
|» » checkin_margin|body|integer \| null|false|How long (in minutes) after the expected checkin time will we wait until we consider the checkin to have been missed.|
|» » max_runtime|body|integer \| null|false|How long (in minutes) is the checkin allowed to run for in CheckInStatus.IN_PROGRESS before it is considered failed. Maximum 10080 (7 days).|

## Delete a Monitor or Monitor Environments for a Project

<a id="opIddeleteProjectMonitor"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/projects/string/string/monitors/string/' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /api/0/projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/monitors/{monitor_id_or_slug}/`

Delete a monitor or monitor environments.

<h3 id="delete-a-monitor-or-monitor-environments-for-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|monitor_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the monitor.|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|

<h3 id="delete-a-monitor-or-monitor-environments-for-a-project-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Accepted|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
auth_token
</aside>

## Retrieve Check-Ins for a Monitor by Project

<a id="opIdlistProjectMonitorCheckins"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/api/0/projects/string/string/monitors/string/checkins/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/0/projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/monitors/{monitor_id_or_slug}/checkins/`

Retrieve a list of check-ins for a monitor

<h3 id="retrieve-check-ins-for-a-monitor-by-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|monitor_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the monitor.|
